Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of flowers. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

They started to go up the hill, but it was very steep and slippery. Lily and Ben had to use their hands and feet to move. They struggled a lot. They got tired and dirty.

"Are we there yet?" Ben asked.

"Not yet, but we are close. Come on, we can do it!" Lily said.

They kept going, but Ben felt sick. He was pale and sweaty. He stopped and sat down.

"Lily, I can't go on. My tummy hurts and my head spins. I want to go back," he said.

Lily looked at him and felt sorry. She wanted to see the other side, but she also wanted to help her friend.

"OK, Ben. We can go back. Maybe we can try again another day. Here, take my hand. I will help you down the hill," she said.

She gave him her hand and they started to go down the hill. They were careful and slow. They saw a pass between two trees. They went through the pass and saw the park again.

They were happy to be back. They saw their mom and dad waiting for them. They ran to them and hugged them.

"Did you have fun, kids?" mom asked.

"Yes, we did. But we also had a problem. We tried to climb the hill, but it was too hard. Ben got sick and we had to go back," Lily said.

"Oh, poor Ben. Are you OK now?" dad asked.

"Yes, I am. Lily helped me. She is a good friend," Ben said.

They smiled at each other. They were proud of themselves. They had a big adventure and they learned a lot. They decided to play in the park for a while and then go home and rest. They knew they would have more fun tomorrow.

Tom and Mia were playing with their toy cars on the floor. They liked to make loud noises as they zoomed and crashed their cars. Tom had a red car and Mia had a blue car.

"Look, my car is faster than yours!" Tom said, pushing his car forward.

"No, mine is faster!" Mia said, pushing her car harder.

They raced their cars across the room, but they did not see the big chair in their way. They both hit the chair with their cars and their cars fell over.

"Ouch!" Tom and Mia said, rubbing their heads.

They looked at their cars and saw that they were broken. The wheels were bent and the doors were loose. They felt sad and angry.

"It's your fault!" Tom said, pointing at Mia.

"No, it's your fault!" Mia said, pointing at Tom.

They started to yell and cry. They did not want to share or say sorry.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken cars and the unhappy children. She frowned and shook her head.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

Tom and Mia stopped crying and looked at Mom. They did not want to tell the truth. They were afraid of getting in trouble.

They were silent.

Mom picked up the cars and examined them. She saw that they were not too badly damaged. She had an idea.

"Maybe we can fix them," Mom said. "But you have to help me. And you have to be nice to each other."

Tom and Mia nodded. They wanted to play with their cars again.

Mom took them to the kitchen and gave them some tools. She showed them how to reverse the wheels and tighten the doors. She helped them glue and tape the parts that were loose.

Soon, the cars looked almost new. Tom and Mia smiled and thanked Mom.

"Can we play with them now?" Tom asked.

"Yes, you can," Mom said. "But remember to be careful and share. And don't make too much noise."

Tom and Mia agreed. They took their cars and went back to the floor. They played nicely and quietly. They took turns and said sorry when they bumped into each other.

They had fun with their cars. And they learned a lesson.

Sam was a soldier. He liked to play with his toy gun and his hat. He pretended to fight bad guys and save his friends. He had a lot of fun.

One day, he saw a big box in the living room. He was very nosy. He wanted to know what was inside. He thought maybe it was a new toy for him. He went to the box and tried to open it.

"Sam, don't touch that!" his mom said. She was angry. "That is not for you. That is for your dad. He is coming home today. He was a real soldier. He was away for a long time. He did a good job. He is very brave."

Sam was surprised. He did not know his dad was a real soldier. He did not know his dad was coming home. He felt bad for opening the box. He said sorry to his mom. He hugged her.

They heard a knock on the door. It was his dad. He had a big smile. He had a big bag. He opened the bag and took out a gift. It was a toy gun and a hat. Just like Sam's. He gave it to Sam.

"Hi, son. I missed you so much. I brought you something. It is a toy gun and a hat. Just like mine. We can play together. We can be soldiers. We can have fun."

Sam was happy. He hugged his dad. He thanked him for the gift. He put on the hat and held the gun. He looked at his dad. He looked like his dad. He felt proud.

The end.

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. One day, she saw a spider on a web. The spider was small and black, with eight legs and shiny eyes. Lily thought the spider was adorable.

She wanted to say hello to the spider. She walked closer to the web and smiled. She said, "Hi, spider. You are very cute. Do you want to be my friend?" She reached out her hand and waved at the spider.

The spider saw Lily and was scared. He did not know who she was or what she wanted. He thought she might hurt him or break his web. He did not want to be her friend. He waved back at her, but not in a friendly way. He waved his legs to tell her to go away.

Lily did not understand the spider. She thought he was waving hello to her. She was happy and waved more. She said, "You are so nice, spider. Can I touch you? Can I play with you?" She moved her hand closer to the web.

The spider was very afraid. He did not want Lily to touch him or play with him. He wanted her to leave him alone. He waved his legs faster and harder. He made a loud noise with his mouth. He said, "No, no, no! Go away, go away, go away!"

Lily heard the spider and was surprised. She did not know he could talk. She did not like his noise. She did not like his waving. She felt sad and scared. She said, "Oh, spider. Why are you so mean? Why don't you like me?" She pulled back her hand and ran away.

The spider was relieved. He saw Lily run away and felt safe. He fixed his web and calmed down. He said, "That was close. That was a big and scary girl. I don't want to see her again. I just want to be alone." He curled up in his web and hoped no one would bother him.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many green needles. Sara said, "This is a pine tree. It smells good." Tom said, "Can I touch it?" Sara said, "Yes, but be careful. The needles are sharp. They can hurt you."

Tom reached out his hand and touched the pine tree. He felt the needles prick his fingers. He said, "Ow! Ow! Ow!" He pulled his hand back and saw some blood. He started to cry. Sara said, "Oh no, Tom! Are you okay?" She ran to him and hugged him.

Sara saw a red bandana in her pocket. She took it out and wrapped it around Tom's hand. She said, "This will make it better. It is red, like your favorite color." Tom stopped crying and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Sara. You are a good friend." Sara said, "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good friend too."

They heard a loud bark. They turned around and saw a big dog running towards them. The dog looked angry and hungry. It showed its teeth and growled. Sara and Tom were scared. They said, "Help! Help! Help!"

A man came running after the dog. He said, "Stop! Stop! Stop!" He caught the dog and put a leash on it. He said, "I'm sorry, kids. He escaped from his yard. He won't bite you. He is just playful." Sara and Tom said, "No, thank you. We don't like this dog. He is scary and mean."

The man said, "I understand. I will take him away. I hope you are not hurt." He walked away with the dog. Sara and Tom said, "Bye, bye. Go away." They held each other's hand and walked back to their mom. They told her what happened. She said, "I'm glad you are safe. You are brave and smart. I love you." She kissed them and gave them a cookie. They said, "We love you too, mom. And we love cookies." They ate the cookies and felt happy.

Ben and Lily were at the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. But they had to be careful, because sometimes there were sharks in the sea.

One day, they saw a big shark swimming near the shore. It had a long fin and sharp teeth. It looked hungry and angry. Ben and Lily were scared. They ran to Mom and Dad and told them about the shark.

Mom and Dad told them to stay on the sand and not go near the water. They called the lifeguard and pointed at the shark. The lifeguard was brave and strong. He had a boat and a net. He went to the water and chased the shark away. He rescued the people and the fish from the shark.

Ben and Lily were happy and relieved. They thanked the lifeguard and gave him a hug. They learned that sharks can be dangerous and that lifeguards can be heroes. They decided to play with their buckets and shovels instead of going to the water. They were still restless, but they were also safe.

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big melon on a table. It is green and round and shiny. They want to eat the melon.

They run to the table and try to pick up the melon. But the melon is too heavy for them. They push and pull and tug, but the melon does not move. They fall on the ground and hurt their knees. They are sad.

A man comes to the table. He is the owner of the melon. He sees Lila and Tom on the ground. He is not angry. He is kind. He picks up the melon and cuts it in half. He gives one half to Lila and one half to Tom. He says, "Here, you can have some of my melon. It is sweet and juicy. I hope you feel better."

Lila and Tom smile. They say, "Thank you, mister. You are nice. We are sorry for trying to take your melon." They eat the melon and feel happy. The melon is sweet and juicy. They share it with the man. They make a new friend. They are not sad anymore.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make them zoom and crash on the carpet. But then, one of the cars stopped moving. Lily picked it up and saw that the battery was empty.

"Ben, we need a new battery for this car," she said.

"Where can we find one?" Ben asked.

"Maybe in the kitchen. Mom has some in a drawer," Lily said.

They ran to the kitchen and opened the drawer. They saw a lot of batteries of different sizes and colors. They grabbed one that looked like the one in the car and ran back to the living room.

Lily tried to put the new battery in the car, but it was too big. It did not fit. She tried to pull it out, but it was stuck. She pulled harder and harder, until she heard a loud pop. The battery exploded and released a lot of smoke and sparks. Lily and Ben were frightened. They dropped the car and ran away, screaming.

"Mom! Mom! Help!" they cried.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the smoke and the sparks and the broken car and the battery. She was angry and scared.

"What did you do?" she asked.

"We wanted a new battery for the car, but it was too big and it popped," Lily said.

"You should never play with batteries. They are dangerous. They can hurt you and start a fire. You are very lucky that nothing worse happened," Mom said.

She took the car and the battery and threw them in the trash. She opened the window to let the smoke out. She hugged Lily and Ben and told them to be more careful next time. She also told them to say sorry to each other and to the car.

Lily and Ben said sorry to each other and to the car. They felt bad for breaking their toy. They decided to play with something else that did not need batteries. They learned their lesson.

Anna was happy to see Brownie, but also sad. She missed his old ear and his old nose. She said, "Mom, why did you change Brownie? I liked him the way he was. He had memory of all the times we played and cuddled. He was important to me."

He still loves you very much. And he is still important to you. The ribbon is a gift from me to show you how much I love you and Brownie."

One day, Sara's mom said they had to go to the store. Sara did not want to go. She wanted to stay with Luna. She begged her mom to let her stay, but her mom said no. She said Luna would be fine, and they would be back soon. She said Sara could bring one toy with her.

They saw a lot of flowers and trees and a small pond with fish. They also saw a dog that was sleeping on a mat. They thought the dog was cute and wanted to pet it. They went closer and said "Hello, doggy!"

But the dog was not happy to see them. It woke up and barked loudly. It ran towards them and showed its teeth. It wanted to bite them and chase them away. Tim and Sam were scared and ran back to the gate. They dropped their ball and left it behind.

They ran home and told their mom what happened. She was not pleased and said "You should not enter other people's yards without asking. That is rude and dangerous. You could have hurt the dog or the flowers or the fish. And you lost your ball too. How would you feel if someone entered your yard and took your things?"

Lila wipes her tears and hugs her teddy bear. She sees that he is still whole and soft.

"I'm sorry, kids. Are you okay?" he asked.

Lily and Tom nodded. They were fine, but they were still scared. They dropped their pistols and hugged each other.

"Thank you, mister. You saved us," they said.

The man smiled and said, "You're welcome, kids. But you should be careful when you play with pistols. They are not toys. They can hurt people and animals. You should play with something else, like balls or dolls or books. They are more fun and safe."

The moral of the story is: Don't break things that are not yours. Be kind and fair with your brother. Chess is not about winning or losing. It is about playing and learning.

Mom hugged Anna and Ben. They were safe but sorry.

"We're sorry, mom," Anna and Ben said. "We didn't listen to you. We went too far. We won't do it again."

Mom smiled. She was glad they were okay.

"I forgive you," mom said. "But you learned a lesson. The unknown can be dangerous. You should always be careful and follow the rules. They are there to protect you."

Anna and Ben nodded. They learned their lesson. They thanked mom and went home. They never went to the unknown again. They were happy with what they had.

Lily thanked the lady and continued playing. She remembered the message of kindness and was more careful with her steps. She didn't want to stumble again and get hurt. From that day on, Lily was more aware of her surroundings and didn't take any careless steps. The end.

Tim went to his mom and told her what happened. She gave him a hug and told him not to worry. They worked together to fix the toy car. Soon, it was back to its normal size. Tim was happy again, and he promised never to play with glue again.

"Tom, where are you?" Lucy called out. Tom jumped out from behind the tree and said, "Meow! Here I am!" Lucy laughed and said, "You are so good at hiding!"

Later, Lucy saw that Tom had a small cut on his leg. She remembered that her mom used cream to help with cuts. She went inside and found the cream. Lucy carefully put the cream on Tom's cut and wiped it with a soft cloth. Tom felt much better.

Lucy's mom saw what she did and was very proud. She said, "Well done, Lucy! You took care of Tom and made him feel better." Lucy smiled and hugged her mom. From that day on, Lucy always helped her friends when they were hurt.

The moral of the story is to always help and care for your friends when they need you.

Together, Fluffy and Chirpy played and sang songs near the big iron. They recorded all of their favorite songs in the small box. When they were done, they sat down and listened to the songs they made. They were very happy and had a great time.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a girl named Lily. Lily had a big bottle of pink shampoo. She loved her shampoo very much. It made her hair soft and shiny.

One day, a boy named Tom came to the village. Tom saw Lily's pink shampoo and wanted it. He said, "Lily, can I have your pink shampoo?" Lily said, "No, it is mine. I love it very much." Tom was sad and angry. He wanted the pink shampoo so badly.

Tom thought of a plan. He said, "Lily, if you marry me, we can share the pink shampoo." Lily thought for a moment. She didn't want to marry Tom, but she wanted to be kind. So, Lily said, "Okay, Tom, we can share my pink shampoo, but we don't need to marry." Tom agreed, and they both used the pink shampoo happily.

Sue and the dog played all day. They were very happy. But the sky was getting dark. Sue knew she had to go home soon. She was a little scared of the dark.

Sue said goodbye to the dog and started to walk home. On her way, she saw a big tree. The tree had long branches that looked like big arms. Sue was very scared of the tree.

As she walked past the tree, the wind blew hard. The tree's branches grabbed Sue's pink skirt and it ripped! Sue cried and ran home without her favorite skirt. The end.

Molly was a 3 year old girl who liked to explore. One day, Molly went to a park. As she wandered around, she spotted a teaspoon. Molly picked it up and called her mom.

"Mommy, Mommy, look what I found!" shouted Molly.

Her mom smiled at her and said, "Why don't you come over to show me?" Molly ran over, with the teaspoon in her hand. Mommy looked at the teaspoon and said, "That's a special spoon, Molly. It's from a far away land."

Molly was amazed and asked what they did with the spoon. Mommy said, "In that land, they use the teaspoon to make a sour drink. Have you ever tried something sour?"

Molly nodded and said she had. "It's yucky but it's fun," Molly said. Mommy smiled and nodded. She said, "Let's go home and see if we can make our own sour drink with this teaspoon!"

And off they went, with Molly holding tight onto the teaspoon, excited to make their own sour drink!

One day, the little boy started to chew on something he had never chewed on before. It was as thin as paper and made a soft crinkly noise every time he chewed it. He didn't know what it was but he couldn't stop chewing it. He chewed and he chewed until his teeth were sore. He soon realised he was chewing on leaves from the trees on the thin street. He smiled and kept on chewing as he made his way home. The end.

The rain kept coming down hard. Suddenly, an ancient oak tree appeared in the distance. Jack ran closer and noticed that the tree was huge! He stood in awe of the tree and felt very small.

Jack smiled as he realised that the rain had a magical power. It made things grow and the tree looked so strong and majestic. Jack was happy for the rain and thanked it for blessing him with the gift of an ancient tree.

Lucy knew that the ugly monster's message was true- rise up and do great things!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to watch the pigeons in the park. She would often feed them bread crumbs and watch them peck away. One day, as she was playing in the park, she noticed a rough-looking man walking towards her.

Lily felt scared and wanted to run away, but then she remembered the pigeons. She quickly grabbed some bread crumbs and threw them towards the man. To her surprise, the man stopped and smiled at her. He reached into his pocket and pulled out a handful of birdseed.

Lily and the man sat together, feeding the pigeons and talking. The man told her stories of his travels and adventures. As the sun began to set, the pigeons started to rise up into the sky, and so did the man. He thanked Lily for her kindness and said goodbye.

From that day on, Lily never judged someone by their appearance and always remembered the power of kindness.

Soon, Benny's mommy and daddy came to save him. They chased the wolf away and Benny was safe. Benny learned that it's important to listen to his mommy, but also to be brave when he needs to be.

The ghost asked Timmy why he looked scared. Timmy told the ghost about the spicy chili and how he didn't like it. The ghost laughed and said that he didn't like spicy food either. Timmy and the ghost became friends and talked for a long time. Timmy wasn't scared anymore and was happy to have a new friend.

As he climbed higher and higher, he noticed that the tree was getting very filthy with mud and leaves. But Bongo didn't care, he just wanted to win the race. Suddenly, Bongo slipped and fell down from the tree. His friends rushed to help him, but it was too late. Bongo had hurt himself badly and couldn't move.

Bongo's friends felt very sad and guilty. They realized that they shouldn't have started the race in the first place. They should have known that climbing trees can be dangerous. From that day on, they promised to always be careful and not take unnecessary risks. The moral of the story is that it's important to think before you act and always be safe.

Max replied, "You're cool too, Lily. Let's jump on the mattress and have fun!" And so, they jumped on the mattress and had a great time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her toys. One day, she found a big barrel in her yard. She climbed inside and pretended she was sailing on a big ship.

Suddenly, her neighbor Tom came over. He was being rude and didn't want to play with Lily. "I don't like you," he said. "You're not fun."

Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. But then she had an idea. She took a piece of paper and signed her name on it. "Tom, will you sign this too?" she asked.

Tom was confused, but he signed the paper anyway. Lily smiled and said, "Now we're friends again!" And they played together in the barrel, sailing on their big ship.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty parrot named Polly. Polly loved to squawk and make noise all day long. One day, Polly's owner asked her to be quiet so he could take a nap. Polly didn't listen and kept squawking loudly.

Suddenly, Polly saw a mouse and whispered to herself, "I want to play with the mouse." But the owner heard her whisper and said, "Polly, you need to be quiet. I'm trying to sleep." Polly felt bad and decided to be quiet for the rest of the day.

From that day on, Polly learned to whisper when she wanted to talk to herself or play with her toys. And her owner was happy that he could finally take a nap without any noise. The end.

His mommy explained that he needed to be clean and smell good. Timmy understood and said, "Okay mommy, I'll take a bath."

When they got home, Timmy took a bath and his mommy helped him wash his hair. Timmy felt clean and happy again. He said, "Mommy, can we go back to the park tomorrow?" His mommy said, "Sure, we can go back and see the happy doggy on the billboard again." Timmy smiled and said, "Yay, happy doggy!"

Lily's mommy helped her kneel down by her bed and they said a prayer together. Then, her mommy tucked her in and gave her a kiss goodnight. Lily felt much better and soon fell asleep. From then on, whenever she had a nightmare, she knew she could kneel down and pray for help.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play in the forest with his friends. One day, Benny saw a big hole in the ground. He wanted to see what was inside, so he hopped closer to it. Suddenly, he fell inside the hole and couldn't escape.

Benny cried for help. His friend, a little bird named Billy, heard him and flew down to the hole. "Benny, are you okay?" Billy asked. "No, I'm stuck!" Benny replied. "Don't worry, I'll help you," Billy said. He flew up to the top of the hole and found a big rock. He brought the rock back and dropped it down the hole. The rock hit the ground and made a loud noise. Benny was scared, but then he saw that the rock had opened a small hole in the side of the big hole. "Billy, you did it! I can escape now!" Benny shouted. He hopped through the small hole and was free again.

"Thanks, Billy! You saved me!" Benny said. "No problem, Benny. I'm happy to help," Billy replied. Benny and Billy continued to play in the forest, but Benny was more careful around big holes from then on.

At the end of the day, only a few fruits remained on Tom's table. He was happy because it was not difficult to sell his fruits today. Tom said, "Thank you, Lily, for helping me sell my fruits." Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom! I like your fruits very much."

Lucy went to Tom and asked, "Why are you sad, Tom?" Tom said, "I want to draw on the blackboard, but I don't have any chalk." Lucy had an idea. She said, "Let's go and borrow some chalk from the teacher."

So, Lucy and Tom went to their teacher, Miss Jane. They asked, "Can we please borrow some chalk to draw on the blackboard?" Miss Jane smiled and said, "Of course! Here you go." She gave them some chalk.

Lucy and Tom went back to the blackboard and started to draw. They drew a big sun, a house, and some flowers. Tom was not sad anymore. They had so much fun drawing together. And when they finished, they returned the chalk to Miss Jane.

"Wow, this is a treasure!" Sam said. "Let's keep it!"

"No, we should return it," Lily said. "Maybe it belongs to someone else. Maybe it is very old and important."

Sam did not listen. He put the stone in his pocket and ran away. Lily followed him, but he was too fast. He got to his bike and rode away.

Lily was sad and angry. She went back to the beach and looked for more stones. She hoped to find another one like Sam's. But she only found ordinary stones and shells.

Then she saw a man walking on the beach. He had a big hat and a long beard. He had a bag full of stones and shells. He looked at Lily and smiled.

"Hello, little girl," he said. "Do you like stones and shells?"

"Yes, I do," Lily said. "But I like to return them to the sand after I play with them."

"That's very good of you," the man said. "You are very kind and respectful. You know, some of these stones and shells are very ancient. They have stories and secrets from long ago. They are not meant to be taken away. They are meant to be shared and admired."

"Really?" Lily said. "Can you tell me some of their stories and secrets?"

"Of course," the man said. "But first, let me show you something. Do you see this stone?" He took out a shiny stone from his bag. It was round and smooth and had strange marks on it. It was the same as Sam's stone.

Lily gasped. "That's the stone that Sam took!" she said.

"Yes, it is," the man said. "And do you know what it is? It is an ancient coin. It was made by a king who ruled this land long ago. He was very greedy and cruel. He wanted to have all the coins in the world. He made his people work hard and pay him a lot of taxes. He hid his coins in a secret cave under the sand. But one day, a big storm came and washed away the sand and the cave. The coins were scattered on the beach. And that's how I found them."

"Wow, that's amazing!" Lily said. "But why did you take them?"

"I took them to study them and learn from them," the man said. "I am a historian. I like to know about the past and how people lived. But I don't keep them for myself. I share them with other people who are interested. I also return them to the beach when I am done. I think that's what the king should have done. He should have shared his wealth and happiness with his people. He would have been a better king and a happier person."

Lily nodded. She understood. She wished Sam would understand too. She hoped he would return the coin to the beach and learn from the man. She thanked the man for telling her the stories and secrets. She said goodbye and went home.

She felt happy and wise. She had learned a lot from the stones and shells. She had learned to be kind and respectful, to share and admire, and to return what was not hers. She had learned the moral value of the story.

They opened one of the mussels and saw a soft and wet thing inside. They thought it was a candy.

"Let's try it, Sam!" Ben said. "Maybe it's sweet!"

They put the soft and wet thing in their mouths. They did not know that it was sour. They thought it was yummy.

They bit the soft and wet thing and made a face. It was not yummy. It was sour and salty and slimy. They spit it out and threw the mussel away.

"Yuck, Ben!" Sam said. "That was not candy! That was gross!"

"Yuck, Sam!" Ben said. "That was not a treasure! That was a trick!"

They heard the boat horn again. It was louder and closer. They looked at the water and saw that it was coming back. It was not playing with them. It was chasing them.

They saw big waves and foam and bubbles. They did not know that it was the tide. They thought it was a monster.

"Run, Sam!" Ben said. "The water monster is coming!"

"Run, Ben!" Sam said. "The boat monster is coming!"

They ran away from the water and the boat. They ran back to the sand and their sand castles. They were scared and wet and sour.

They hugged each other and said sorry.

"Sorry, Sam," Ben said. "I should have listened to the boat."

"Sorry, Ben," Sam said. "I should have looked at the water."

They learned their lesson. They never ran to the water or the boat again. They played at the beach with their sand castles, their holes, and their crabs. They were happy and safe and sweet.

True was his best friend. He was a dog, but not a real dog. He was a dog that only Sam could see and talk to. True was always with Sam, and he helped him when he was sad or scared. True was very important to Sam.

One day, Sam and his mom went to the park. Sam brought his ball and his hat. He wanted to play with True. He threw the ball and said, "Fetch, True!" But True did not come back. Sam looked around and saw a big boy holding his ball. The boy was mean. He said, "This is my ball now. Go away, baby."

Sam felt angry and sad. He wanted his ball back. He wanted True to help him. He said, "Give me my ball. That's not yours. That's mine and True's." The boy laughed. He said, "Who is True? You don't have a friend. You're just a liar."

Sam felt tears in his eyes. He wished True was real. He wished True could bite the boy and make him give the ball back. He closed his eyes and imagined very hard. He imagined True was big and strong and fierce. He imagined True was by his side, ready to protect him.

Then he heard a bark. He opened his eyes and saw True. True was real. He was a real dog. He had brown fur and black spots and a red collar. He looked just like Sam imagined him. He jumped on the boy and made him drop the ball. He growled and showed his teeth. The boy ran away, crying.

Sam was amazed. He hugged True and said, "You're here. You're real. You're my friend." True licked his face and wagged his tail. He barked and said, "I'm always here. I'm always real. I'm always your friend."

Sam smiled and said, "Thank you, True. You're the best." He picked up his ball and his hat. He ran to his mom and said, "Mom, look! This is True. He's my dog. He's my best friend. He's very important to me."

His mom looked surprised. She said, "Where did he come from? How did you find him?" Sam said, "I imagined him. I imagined him very hard. And he came true." His mom smiled and said, "That's amazing, Sam. You have a very special gift. You can make your dreams come true."

Sam nodded and said, "Yes, I can. And I'm very happy." He held True's paw and said, "Come on, True. Let's go play. Let's imagine more things." True barked and said, "Yes, let's go. Let's imagine more things." And they did.

They took the ball outside and started to roll it, toss it, and bounce it. They had a lot of fun with their new toy. But then, they noticed something strange. The ball started to spin faster and faster, and the colors became brighter and brighter. It made a loud humming noise that hurt their ears.

"Stop, stop!" Lila shouted. "It's too loud! It's too fast! What's happening?"

"I don't know!" Ben said. "Maybe it's a magic ball! Maybe it's going to explode!"

They ran away from the ball, scared and confused. They hid behind a tree and watched as the ball spun out of control. It looked like a rainbow firework in the sky.

But then, they heard a voice coming from the hut. It was a man with a big beard and a funny hat. He was holding a remote control in his hand.

"Ha ha ha!" he laughed. "You fell for my trap, you little brats! That was not a gift from the fairies, that was my original invention! The spinning ball of doom! I left it in your hut to lure you out and scare you away! This is my woods now, and you are not welcome here!"

Lila and Ben were shocked and angry. They did not like the mean man who tricked them and took their hut. They wanted to get their toy back and make him go away.

They looked at each other and nodded. They had a plan. They waited until the man was busy admiring his spinning ball of doom. Then, they sneaked up behind him and grabbed his remote control. They pushed all the buttons and made the ball spin faster and faster, until it flew out of his hand and hit him on the head. He fell to the ground, groaning and dizzy.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he cried. "What have you done, you little monsters? You ruined my invention! You ruined my plan! You ruined my day!"

Lila and Ben laughed and cheered. They had won. They took their ball and ran back to their hut. They decided to keep it as a souvenir, but never to play with it again. They learned their lesson. They knew that not all things that are shiny and pretty are good. And they knew that not all people who leave things in their hut are nice. They were happy to have each other and their original hut in the woods.

They went back to the rug and looked at it with new eyes. They did not see traffic anymore. They saw a kingdom full of magic and adventure. They saw castles and forests, dragons and fairies, treasures and secrets. They saw a jolly land where they could do anything they imagined.

They forgot about their cars and their game. They started to play a new game, where they were the heroes of their own story. They had a lot of fun. They liked their jolly land. They did not care about traffic.

Tom and Jen watch the show and clap their hands. They think the lion and the mouse are funny and smart. But some kids behind them are not nice. They talk loud and make noise. They say the lion and the mouse are silly and boring. They throw popcorn and candy at the stage. They are ignorant. They do not care about the show or the people.

Tom and Jen are angry and sad. They want to enjoy the show, but the kids behind them ruin it. They tell their moms, but their moms do not hear them. They struggle to ignore the kids, but they cannot. They feel bad.

Then, something happens. The lion on the stage roars and jumps. He looks at the kids behind Tom and Jen. He is angry too. He says, "Stop it! You are rude and mean. You do not respect the show or the theater. You should be quiet and listen. Or you should leave. Or I will come and get you!"

The kids behind Tom and Jen are scared. They stop talking and making noise. They sit still and quiet. They look at the lion and the mouse. They feel ashamed.

Tom and Jen are happy and proud. They smile and cheer. They say, "Thank you, lion! Thank you, mouse! You are brave and kind. You teach the kids a lesson. You save the show and the theater. You are the best!"

The lion and the mouse bow and smile. They say, "You are welcome, Tom and Jen! You are good and polite. You appreciate the show and the theater. You are our friends!"

The end.

Anna liked to play with her shadow. She would run and jump and make funny shapes with her body. Her shadow would follow her and copy her. Sometimes, Anna would pretend that her shadow was her friend and talk to it.

One day, Anna went to the park with her mom. She saw a big tree with many leaves. She ran to the tree and looked for her shadow. But she could not find it. The tree was so big that it blocked the sun. Anna felt sad. She wanted to play with her shadow.

"Mom, where is my shadow?" Anna asked.

"Your shadow is hiding, sweetie. It is afraid of the tree. The tree is very old and ancient. It has seen many things and knows many stories. Maybe it can tell you one, if you are nice to it." Mom said.

Anna was curious. She wanted to hear a story from the tree. She walked closer to the trunk and touched it gently. She felt the rough bark and the tiny bumps. She whispered, "Hello, tree. Can you tell me a story?"

The tree did not answer. But Anna heard a soft rustle in the leaves. She looked up and saw a bird. The bird was blue and yellow and had a long tail. It sang a beautiful song. Anna smiled. She liked the bird.

The bird flew down and landed on Anna's shoulder. It said, "Hello, little girl. I am the tree's friend. I can tell you a story, if you like. It is a story about how the tree and I met."

Anna nodded eagerly. She wanted to hear the story. The bird said, "It was a long time ago, when I was a baby. I fell out of my nest and hurt my wing. I could not fly. I was scared and alone. Then I saw the tree. It was young and green and had many flowers. It offered me a place to rest and heal. It gave me water and food and shade. It was very kind and gentle. It became my home and my family. We have been together ever since."

Anna listened to the story with wonder. She felt happy for the bird and the tree. She said, "That is a lovely story. Thank you for sharing it with me. You and the tree are very lucky to have each other."

The bird nodded and said, "You are welcome, little girl. You are very polite and friendly. You can come and visit us anytime. We like you."

Anna hugged the bird and said, "I like you too. You are my new friends. Can I play with you?"

The bird said, "Of course you can. But first, you have to wash your hands. They are dirty from touching the tree. The tree does not mind, but your mom might."

Anna laughed and said, "Okay, I will wash my hands. Then we can play. Maybe we can find my shadow too. It must be lonely without me."

The bird said, "I think your shadow is waiting for you behind the tree. It is shy, but it likes you too. It wants to play with you."

Anna ran to the other side of the tree and saw her shadow. It was waving at her. Anna waved back and said, "Hello, shadow. I missed you. Let's play together."

The shadow nodded and said, "Hello, Anna. I missed you too. Let's play together."

Anna, the bird, and the shadow played happily under the ancient tree. They had a lot of fun. Mom watched them and smiled. She was glad that Anna had made new friends. She thought that the park was a magical place.

Their mom hugged them and said, "I love you too, Tom and Lily. I know you are good children. But you have to listen to me and follow the rules. Lollipops are not for every day. They are for special occasions. Now, let's pick up the lollipops and see if we can save some. Maybe we can share them with your friends later."

One day, they found a big closet in the bedroom. They opened the door and saw many old clothes and toys. They tried on some hats and coats and pretended to be different people. They had a lot of fun.

Suddenly, they heard a voice from inside the closet. It said, "Who are you? This is my closet. I own these things."

Ben and Lily were surprised and scared. They looked around and saw a white shape floating in the air. It had two eyes, a nose, and a mouth, but no body. It was a ghost!

"Hello, ghost," Ben said. "We are Ben and Lily. We are sorry, we did not know this was your closet. We were just playing."

The ghost looked at them and smiled. It said, "It's okay, I don't mind. I like playing too. I have been alone in this house for a long time. Do you want to be my friends?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They were not scared anymore. They thought the ghost was nice and lonely. They said, "Yes, we want to be your friends. What is your name?"

The ghost said, "My name is Sam. I used to live in this house when I was a boy. But then I got sick and died. Now I stay here with my things. But I don't see anyone else. I'm happy you came."

Ben and Lily felt sorry for Sam. They said, "We're sorry you died, Sam. That's very sad. But we're happy we met you. Can we come and play with you again?"

Sam said, "Yes, please. I would like that very much. You can come and play with me anytime. I have many stories to tell you and games to show you. You are my new friends."

Ben and Lily smiled. They hugged Sam and said, "You are our new friend too, Sam. We will come and play with you again soon. Goodbye for now."

They left the closet and the house. They ran back to their home and told their mom about their adventure. She did not believe them, but they did not care. They knew they had found a special friend in the empty house. A friend who was a ghost.

So Tommy grabbed his measuring cup and started to measure. He was having so much fun. But then, the cup was too full. Tommy couldn't believe it. So he gave it a big hard shake and then a bunch of sugar spilled all over the kitchen floor! 

Mommy was not happy. She looked down at the sugar and then she looked at Tommy. She screamed and yelled so loud that Tommy was scared. He ran way and hid in his bedroom.

Mommy was still very unhappy but when she found Tommy she was so glad. She hugged him and said it was okay. And then she helped him clean up the mess. They worked together and soon the kitchen was all clean. 

Tommy learned an important lesson. Next time he would be sure to measure carefully and not to yell.

Just then, a big, scary man suddenly appeared. He had a big smile on his face. He said, "I'm here to make sure nobody can get in the closet. I will keep all the surprises inside safe."

The man grabbed Lucy and pushed her away from the closet. He then shut the closet door and locked it again. Lucy started to cry. She wanted to know what was inside the closet so badly.

The man laughed and said, "I'm never going to let you open the closet. The secret inside is too precious and must stay hidden. Farewell, little one!"

And so Lucy never found out what was hidden in the soft closet. She spent her days wondering what could be so special. She never found out.

The rabbit took a tiny pair of scissors and very carefully began to cut the pants. The bald man held his breath as the rabbit worked. After a few minutes, the rabbit had finished! The man said "Wow! That was brilliant! Thank you so much, my fluffy white friend!"

The man now had two shorts, and was very happy. He and his pet walked back home, feeling much better. From then on, the man always took his pet along on his walks, just in case he ever split his pants again!

"I'm sorry, Ben," Lily said. She ran to him and hugged him. "I didn't mean to hit you. Are you okay?"

Ben nodded. He hugged her back. "I'm okay, Lily. It was an accident. Don't worry."

They looked at the car on the floor. It had a dent on the roof and a scratch on the door.

"Maybe we should stop playing with the cars," Lily said. "They are too noisy and dangerous."

"Maybe we should go to bed," Ben said. "We are too sleepy and clumsy."

They agreed. They put the cars away and went to their room. They brushed their teeth and put on their pajamas. They climbed into their beds and said good night to each other.

They closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of cars and ceilings and hugs.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Lily went first. She slid down fast and laughed. Ben followed her. He slid down faster and shouted.

"Look, Lily, a bear!" Ben said. He pointed to a big brown animal near the trees. Lily looked and saw the bear too. It was walking slowly and sniffing the air.

"Is it a nice bear?" Lily asked. She felt scared.

"I don't know. Maybe it is hungry. We should go away," Ben said. He took Lily's hand and they ran to their mom.

"Mom, mom, there is a bear in the park!" Ben said.

"A bear? Where?" Mom asked. She looked around and saw the bear too. It was coming closer to the slide.

"Quick, kids, get in the car!" Mom said. She opened the door and helped Lily and Ben inside. She closed the door and locked it.

The bear reached the slide and climbed on it. It slid down slowly and growled. It saw the car and walked to it. It scratched the door and tried to open it. But it could not. It gave up and walked away.

Lily and Ben watched the bear leave. They hugged their mom and felt safe.

Lily did not think it would be fun. She shook her head and hid behind her mom.

Lily did not want to look beautiful. She wanted to look like herself. She did not want to change.

Lily liked princesses. She liked their dresses and their crowns and their castles. She took the sticker and looked at it.

"Okay," she said softly. "I will try a haircut."

Sue was happy. She said, "Good girl, Lily. Come, sit on this chair. I will be gentle. You can hold your mom's hand if you want."

Lily sat on the chair. She held her mom's hand. She felt the cape around her neck. She saw herself in the mirror. She saw Sue pick up the scissors.

She closed her eyes. She heard the snip, snip, snip of the scissors. She felt the hair fall on the cape. She felt the comb brush her hair. She felt the spray wet her hair.

She opened her eyes. She saw herself in the mirror. She saw her hair. It was shorter and smoother and shinier. It looked different.

She looked at her mom. Her mom smiled and said, "Wow, Lily, you look amazing. You look like a princess."

Lily looked at Sue. Sue smiled and said, "You did great, Lily. You were very brave. How do you like your haircut?"

Lily touched her hair. She felt the softness and the lightness. She felt the sticker on her shirt. She felt the smile on her face.

She liked her haircut. She liked how she looked. She liked how she felt.

She said, "Thank you, Sue. I like my haircut. I feel like a princess."

She became happy. She gave Sue a hug. She gave her mom a hug. She gave herself a hug.

She left the salon with her mom. She waved goodbye to Sue. She looked at the sky and the sun and the birds.

She felt the wind in her hair. She felt the joy in her heart. She felt the princess in her soul.

Sara and Tom like to play in the forest. They look for animals and flowers and mushrooms. One day, they find a big mushroom with red dots. Sara wants to pick it, but Tom says no.

"That is a fairy mushroom," he says. "Fairies live under it. If you pick it, they will be angry."

Sara does not believe him. She thinks he is making it up. She reaches for the mushroom, but Tom pulls her back.

"Look," he says. "There is a fairy. She is coming out of the mushroom."

Sara and Tom see a tiny girl with wings and a dress. She has a crown of flowers on her head. She looks at Sara and Tom with a frown. She says something, but they cannot hear her.

"She is deaf," Tom says. "She cannot hear us. We have to bow to her. That is how we say sorry."

Tom bows to the fairy. He hopes she will forgive them. Sara bows too, but she is still curious. She wants to touch the fairy. She reaches out her hand, but the fairy flies away.

"Bye, fairy," Tom says. "We are sorry. We will not touch your mushroom."

Sara and Tom go back to their home. They tell their mom about the fairy. She smiles and hugs them.

"That is a wonderful story," she says. "But remember, do not pick mushrooms in the forest. Some of them are bad for you."

Sara and Tom nod. They are happy. They have seen a fairy. They hope to see her again.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a carrot nose. They give him a name. They call him Bob.

"Bob is our friend," Lily says. "He is very nice and cold."

"Yes, he is," Tom says. "But he needs something more. He needs eyes and a mouth."

Tom runs to the house. He gets two buttons and some salt. He comes back to the snowman. He puts the buttons on his face. He makes a smile with the salt.

"Look, Lily," Tom says. "Now Bob can see and talk. He is happy."

Lily looks at the snowman. She likes his smile. She thinks the salt looks tasty. She wants to try it. She reaches for the snowman's mouth.

"Stop, Lily," Tom says. "That is not food. That is salt. It is bad for you. It will make you sick."

But Lily does not listen. She is curious. She takes some salt in her hand. She puts it in her mouth.

"Yuck!" Lily says. "This is not tasty. This is bitter and ouchy. It hurts my tongue."

She spits out the salt. She makes a face. She starts to cry.

Tom feels sorry for Lily. He hugs her. He helps her wipe her mouth.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tom says. "I should have told you before. Salt is not for eating. It is for making snowmen smile."

Lily stops crying. She hugs Tom back. She smiles.

"It's okay, Tom," Lily says. "I learned my lesson. Salt is not tasty. It is for Bob. He likes it."

They look at the snowman. He still has his smile. He seems to wink at them.

"Bob is a good friend," Lily says. "He is very nice and cold. And he has a funny smile."

"Yes, he is," Tom says. "And he has a funny name. Bob."

They laugh. They play with Bob. They have fun in the snow.

"Can we get the mail, mom?" Anna asks.

"Sure, but be careful. The road is busy. Hold hands and look both ways," mom says.

Anna and Ben nod and run to the mailbox. They open the little door and see a lot of letters and a big package. The package is for dad. It is from his work.

"Wow, this is heavy!" Ben says. He tries to lift the package, but it is too hard.

"Let me help you," Anna says. She grabs the other side of the package. Together, they manage to pull it out of the mailbox.

"Good job, twins!" mom says. She comes to meet them and takes the package and the letters. "This is very nice of you. Dad will be happy to see his package."

Anna and Ben smile. They are proud of themselves. They like to help and they like to get the mail.

Lily and Ben were twins who lived in a big city. They liked to explore new places and play with their toys. One day, they saw a big red bus that looked very unique. It had pictures of animals and flowers on it.

"Wow, look at that bus!" Lily said. "It is so pretty and different. Can we go inside?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it is not for us. Maybe it is for someone else."

But Lily was curious and did not listen to Ben. She ran to the bus and opened the door. She saw many seats and windows and a big wheel. She climbed on a seat and pretended to drive the bus.

"Beep beep! I am a bus driver!" she shouted. "Come on, Ben, join me!"

Ben was scared and did not want to go inside. He saw a man in a blue uniform walking towards the bus. He looked angry and had a badge on his chest.

"Hey, you!" the man yelled. "What are you doing in my bus? This is not a toy, this is a special bus for the zoo. You are not allowed to touch it. Get out of there right now!"

Lily heard the man and felt scared too. She jumped off the seat and ran to Ben. The man followed them and grabbed their arms.

"You are very naughty children," he said. "You could have broken something or hurt yourself. I am going to punish you. I am going to take you to your parents and tell them what you did. They will be very angry with you."

Lily and Ben started to cry. They wished they had not gone inside the bus. They wished they had listened to Ben. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect other people's things and not to be too curious. They learned that some things are not for playing, even if they look unique.

One day, Ben falls down and hurts his knee. He cries and Sam stops. Sam runs back to Ben and helps him up. He says, "Are you okay, Ben? Do you want to go home?"

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys in the park. One day, they see a big red wagon. It has four wheels and a long rope. Lily and Ben want to ride in the wagon.

"Can we share the wagon?" Lily asks Ben.

"Yes, we can. You sit in the wagon and I pull the rope. Then we switch," Ben says.

Lily and Ben smile. They are happy to share. Lily climbs in the wagon and Ben pulls the rope. They go around the park. They see birds, flowers and trees. They have fun.

After a while, Ben says, "It's my turn to sit in the wagon. You pull the rope."

Lily nods. She gets out of the wagon and Ben gets in. She takes the rope and pulls the wagon. But the wagon is heavy. Lily has to pull hard. She gets tired.

"Ben, the wagon is heavy. Can you help me pull?" Lily asks.

"No, I don't want to. You pull. I sit," Ben says.

Lily feels sad. Ben is not nice. He does not share. He does not help. Lily stops pulling. She lets go of the rope. The wagon rolls down the hill. Ben screams. He falls out of the wagon. He gets dirty.

Lily runs to Ben. She sees that he is not hurt. But he is covered in mud. He cries.

"I'm sorry, Ben. Are you okay?" Lily asks.

Ben looks at Lily. He sees that she is clean. He feels sorry. He says, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was mean. I did not share. I did not help. Can you forgive me?"

Lily smiles. She says, "Yes, I forgive you. But next time, we have to share and help. That's what friends do."

Ben nods. He says, "You're right. That's what friends do. Thank you, Lily. You're a good friend."

Lily and Ben hug. They are friends again. They learn a lesson. Sharing and helping are good. Being mean and selfish are bad. They go home. They wash the mud off. They are clean and happy. The end.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big brown dog. The dog has a chain around his neck. He looks sad.

"Hello, dog," Lily says. "Why are you sad?"

The dog does not answer. He just looks at Lily and Ben with big eyes.

"Maybe he is lonely," Ben says. "Maybe he wants to play with us."

Lily and Ben go closer to the dog. They are not afraid. They are kind. They touch the dog's fur. It is soft and warm. The dog wags his tail. He likes Lily and Ben.

"Can we play with you, dog?" Lily asks. "We can throw a ball for you. Or we can run with you. Or we can give you a hug."

The dog barks. He sounds happy. He nods his head. He wants to play with Lily and Ben.

Lily and Ben smile. They are happy too. They find a ball and throw it for the dog. The dog runs after the ball. He catches it and brings it back. He drops it at Lily and Ben's feet. He wants them to throw it again.

They play for a long time. They have fun. The dog is not sad anymore. He is happy. He has new friends. Lily and Ben are happy too. They have a new friend. They love the big brown dog. And the big brown dog loves them.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play in the woods. She had a big brother, Tom, who always warned her to stay away from the old house. He said it was dangerous and scary. But Lily was curious and foolish. She wanted to see what was inside the old house.

One day, when Tom was at school, Lily sneaked out of her home and ran to the woods. She found the old house and opened the door. It was dark and dusty. She saw a big chest in the corner. She wondered what was in it. She walked to the chest and lifted the lid.

Suddenly, a loud roar came from the chest. A big, hairy monster jumped out and grabbed Lily. It had sharp teeth and claws. It was angry and hungry. Lily screamed and tried to run away, but it was too late. The monster bit her and dragged her into the chest. The lid slammed shut.

Tom came home from school and looked for Lily. He saw her footprints in the woods and followed them. He reached the old house and heard a muffled cry from the chest. He ran to the chest and opened the lid. He saw the monster and Lily. Lily was hurt and bleeding. She looked at Tom and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I should have listened to you." Then she closed her eyes and stopped breathing.

Tom was sad and angry. He tried to fight the monster, but it was too strong. It pushed him away and closed the lid. Tom ran back to his home and told his parents what happened. They called the police and the hunters, but they could not find the monster or the chest. They only found Lily's shoe and a drop of blood.

The moral of the story is: listen to your elders and don't go to dangerous places. Curiosity can kill you.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lila had a rubber duck that squeaked when she squeezed it. Ben had a toy car that made noises and flashed lights when he pushed a button.

"Look at my car, Lila!" Ben said. "It goes vroom vroom and blink blink!"

Lila looked at Ben's car and smiled. She liked the bright colors and the sounds. She squeezed her duck and made it squeak.

"Look at my duck, Ben!" Lila said. "It goes quack quack and is soft and yellow!"

Ben looked at Lila's duck and frowned. He did not like the duck. He thought it was boring and silly. He wanted Lila to play with his car.

"Your duck is no fun, Lila!" Ben said. "Give me your duck and you can have my car!"

Lila did not want to give Ben her duck. She loved her duck and hugged it tight. She did not want Ben's car. She thought it was loud and scary.

"No, Ben!" Lila said. "I want to keep my duck! You keep your car!"

Ben was angry. He reached for Lila's duck and tried to take it from her. Lila pulled back and cried.

"We were playing with our toys, Mom," Ben said. "But I wanted Lila's duck and she wanted my car."

"And we did not want to share, Mom," Lila said. "But we made each other sad and mad."

One day, they decided to display their maze to their mom and dad. They invited them to their room and showed them their cars and their maze. They said, "Look, mom and dad, this is our maze. We made it ourselves. It is very interesting. Do you want to see how our cars go through it?"

Mom and dad smiled and said, "Yes, we do. Your maze looks very impressive. How do you play with it?"

Ben and Lily explained, "We take turns to pick a car and put it in the maze. Then we try to find the way out. Sometimes we get stuck and have to go back. Sometimes we find a shortcut. Sometimes we bump into each other. It is very fun."

Mom and dad said, "That sounds very fun. Can we try it too?"

Ben and Lily said, "Sure, you can. But be careful, the maze is tricky. You might get lost."

Mom and dad picked a car each and put it in the maze. They followed the paper tubes and tried to find the exit. They had fun, but they also got confused. They went in circles and crossed paths. They could not find the way out.

Ben and Lily watched them and giggled. They knew the maze very well. They knew a secret. There was a hidden door in the box that led to the outside. Follow our voices and we will show you the way out."

Mom and dad listened and followed their voices. They reached the hidden door and saw Ben and Lily waiting for them. They said, "Wow, you tricked us. You made a secret door. That was very clever."

Ben and Lily said, "Thank you. We hope you liked our maze. We had fun making it and playing with it. Do you want to play again?"

Mom and dad said, "Yes, we do. But this time, we want to know the secret too."

Tom said, "Can we keep this rock? Maybe we can sell it and buy lots of candy and toys!"

Lily said, "Yes, let's keep it. But we have to hide it from the other kids. They might want to take it from us."

They put the rock in Lily's backpack and ran home. They were very happy and excited. They dreamed of all the things they could do with their diamond.

But when they got home, they smelled something bad. They opened Lily's backpack and saw that the rock was not a diamond. It was a piece of cheese. It was very old and very smelly. It had made Lily's backpack and everything in it stinky.

Lily and Tom were very sad and very mad. They threw the cheese in the trash and washed their hands. They said, "This is the worst day ever. We thought we had a diamond, but we only had a cheese."

They learned a lesson. They learned that not everything that shines is a diamond. And they learned that they should not take things that are not theirs. They decided to be more careful and more honest next time. They hugged and said, "We are still best friends. And we still have our dreams."

She took it out and unwrapped it. It was a shiny red candy, and it smelled sweet. Lily put it in her mouth and bit it. It was very hard and sour. Lily made a face and spit it out. It was not a candy, it was a cough drop!

Lily heard her mom coming from the kitchen. She quickly put the cough drop back in the purse and zipped it up. She tried to act normal, but her mom noticed her sour face.

"Lily, what's wrong? Did you eat something bad?" her mom asked.

Lily felt guilty and scared. She did not want to lie, but she did not want to get in trouble. She decided to tell the truth.

"Mom, I'm sorry. I looked in your purse and I took a candy. But it was not a candy, it was a cough drop. It was very yucky. I'm sorry, mom. I won't do it again." Lily said.

Her mom hugged her and smiled. She was not angry, but she was glad that Lily was honest.

"Lily, thank you for telling me the truth. I'm not mad at you, but you should not look in my purse without asking. It is not polite, and it is not safe. You could find something that is not for you, or that could hurt you. Like the cough drop. It is not a candy, it is a medicine. It is for when I have a sore throat. It is not for you. Do you understand?" her mom said.

Lily nodded and said sorry again. She learned her lesson. She did not wonder about her mom's purse anymore. She wondered about other things, but she always asked before touching them. She knew that honesty was the best policy, and that curiosity should be careful.

Lily was a gifted girl who loved to draw and paint. She had many colors and brushes and papers to make beautiful pictures. She liked to share her pictures with her friends and family.

One day, she wanted to draw a lime, a green fruit that was sour and juicy. She looked for a lime in the kitchen, but she could not find any. She asked her mom, "Mom, do we have any limes?"

Her mom said, "No, dear, we don't have any limes right now. Why do you need a lime?"

Lily said, "I want to draw a lime. I need to see a lime to draw it well."

Her mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily, but we can't go to the store today. Maybe you can draw something else, or use your imagination."

Lily was sad. She really wanted to draw a lime. She thought, maybe I can find a lime outside. She put on her shoes and coat and went to the backyard. She looked around, but she did not see any limes. She saw a lemon tree, but the lemons were yellow, not green. She saw a lime tree, but the limes were not ripe yet. They were small and green and hard.

She thought, maybe I can pick one of the small limes and draw it. She reached for a lime, but she heard a voice.

"Stop! Don't pick that lime!" the voice said.

Lily looked around and saw a bird on the lime tree. The bird was blue and yellow and had a long tail. It was a parrot.

"Why not?" Lily asked.

"Because that lime is not ready. It needs more time and sun and water to grow big and juicy. If you pick it now, you will prevent it from becoming a good lime. And you will also prevent me from eating it later. I love limes. They are my favorite fruit."

Lily was surprised. She did not know that parrots could talk. She also did not know that parrots liked limes.

"I'm sorry, Mr. Parrot. I did not mean to hurt your lime. I just wanted to draw it. I like limes too. They are pretty and sour."

The parrot said, "It's okay, little girl. I understand. You are gifted. You can draw many things. But you don't need to pick a lime to draw it. You can use your memory and your imagination. You can also look at a picture of a lime in a book or on a screen. That way, you can draw a lime and also let the lime grow and be happy."

Lily thought about what the parrot said. She realized that he was right. She did not need to pick a lime to draw it. She could use other ways to see a lime. She also did not want to prevent the lime from growing or the parrot from eating it.

She said, "Thank you, Mr. Parrot. You are very smart and kind. I will not pick the lime. I will use my memory and my imagination to draw it. And I will also draw you. You are very beautiful and colorful."

The parrot said, "You are welcome, little girl. You are very sweet and polite. I will be happy to see your drawing. And I will also share a lime with you when they are ripe. They are very tasty and good for you."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mr. Parrot. That sounds very nice. I will come back to see you and the limes. Goodbye for now."

The parrot said, "Goodbye, little girl. Have fun drawing."

Lily went back to her house and got her colors and brushes and papers. She drew a lime and a parrot and showed them to her mom. Her mom was very proud and happy. She said, "Lily, you are very gifted. You can draw a lime and a parrot without picking them. You are also very respectful and caring. You did not prevent the lime from growing or the parrot from eating it. You are a good girl."

Lily hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I learned a lot today. I learned that limes are not ready yet, that parrots can talk, and that I can use my memory and my imagination to draw. I also learned that I should not prevent others from being happy. I should share and be kind."

Her mom said, "You are very welcome, Lily. I'm glad you learned so much. You are a smart and good girl. I love you very much."

Lily said, "I love you too, mom. And I love limes and parrots too."

The end.

Tom does not listen. He thinks it is fun to chase Mia with his truck and his needle. He drives his truck towards Mia and her doll.

"Beep, beep, beep! Move, Mia, move! My truck is hungry. It wants to eat your doll," Tom says, laughing.

But Tom does not stop. He follows Mia to the couch and tries to climb on it too. He still has his truck and his needle in his hands.

"Come on, Mia, don't be a baby. Let me play with your doll. My truck is very hungry. It needs to eat something," Tom says, reaching for the pillow.

Mia is very angry. She does not want to play with Tom anymore. She wants him to go away and leave her and her doll alone. She sees a book on the couch. It is big and heavy. She has an idea. She grabs the book and throws it at Tom.

"Take that, Tom! You are not strong. You are silly. You can't eat my doll. You can only eat food," Mia says, hitting Tom with the book.

Tom is surprised. He feels a pain in his head. He drops his truck and his needle. He starts to cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! That hurts, Mia. That is not nice. You are mean, Mia. You made me cry," Tom says, rubbing his head.

Mia does not feel sorry for Tom. She thinks he deserves it. She hugs her doll and smiles.

"Good, Tom. Now you know how I feel. Maybe next time you will be nice and play with your own toys," Mia says, sticking out her tongue.

One night, Ben and his mom went to the park. They wanted to see the owls that lived in the trees. Ben loved owls. He liked their big eyes and soft feathers.

"Look, mom, there is an owl!" Ben said, pointing to a branch. "Can we feed it?"

Mom shook her head. "No, Ben, we can't feed the owl. The owl is not hungry. The owl hunts for its own food. It eats mice and bugs and other small animals. That is what owls do."

Ben felt sad. He wanted to be friends with the owl. He wanted to give it something nice to eat. He looked around the park. He saw a bag of popcorn on a bench. Someone had left it there. Maybe the owl would like some popcorn.

"Mom, can I give the owl some popcorn?" Ben asked. "Popcorn is yummy and crunchy. And it is available. No one is eating it."

Mom smiled. She knew Ben was trying to be kind. But she also knew that popcorn was not good for owls. She explained to Ben that owls need different food than people. Popcorn could make them sick or choke them.

"Popcorn is not good for owls, Ben. It is good for people. But owls need meat and bones and fur. That is what makes them strong and healthy. Popcorn is not available for owls. It is only available for people."

Ben understood. He did not want to hurt the owl. He wanted to help it. He put the popcorn back on the bench. He waved to the owl and said, "Bye, owl. I hope you find some good food tonight. Maybe we can see you again."

The owl blinked and hooted. It seemed to say, "Bye, Ben. Thank you for being nice. Maybe we can see you again too."

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for worms. They had a big jar where they kept the worms they found. They wanted to make a worm farm.

"Look, I found a big worm!" Lily said, holding up a long, slimy worm. "He is so wiggly and shiny!"

"Let me see!" Ben said, reaching for the worm. "Wow, he is bigger than the others. Can I put him in the jar?"

"Okay, but be careful. He might try to escape," Lily said, handing him the worm. Ben opened the jar and dropped the worm inside. He closed the lid and locked it with a twist.

"There, now he is safe and happy with his friends," Ben said, smiling. He put the jar on the table and went back to digging.

Lily followed him, but she felt a little sad. She liked the big worm. She wanted to hold him again. She looked at the jar and saw the worm moving around. He did not look happy. He looked dull and bored.

She waited until Ben was busy with another worm. Then she tiptoed to the table and picked up the jar. She tried to open the lid, but it was locked. She twisted and pulled, but it did not budge.

"Ben, how do you open this?" she asked, frustrated.

"You don't," Ben said, looking up. "It's locked. That's how we keep the worms inside."

"But I want to see the big worm. He looks sad. Maybe he wants to go back to the dirt," Lily said, holding the jar close to her chest.

"No, he doesn't. He likes it here. He has food and water and friends. Trust me, he is fine," Ben said, digging again.

Lily did not trust him. She felt sorry for the big worm. She decided to find a way to open the jar. She looked around and saw a rock. She had an idea. She took the rock and hit the jar with it. She hoped it would break the lid.

But it did not. It broke the jar. The glass shattered and the worms fell out. The big worm wriggled away into the grass. Lily gasped and dropped the rock. Ben heard the noise and turned around. He saw the broken jar and the worms. He was angry.

"Lily, what did you do?" he shouted. "You broke the jar! You let the worms out!"

"I'm sorry, Ben. I just wanted to help the big worm. He looked dull and unhappy. I wanted to set him free," Lily said, crying.

"Well, you did. You set him all free. Now we have no worm farm. We have nothing," Ben said, stomping his feet.

He picked up a piece of glass and threw it on the ground. It made a loud sound. Lily flinched and sobbed. She wished she had not broken the jar. She wished she had listened to Ben. She wished she had left the big worm alone.

The baby was worried for Mommy and ran out to help her. He wanted to prevent the tide from hurting her. He used all of his strength to push back the tide.

The baby was a hero that day. He saved Mommy from the tide. The mommy was happy and so was the baby.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane. She was having a big birthday party with lots of presents and people around. Jane was very excited, but when she looked outside the window, she saw something strange. All the birds had turned black! 

Jane was shocked and began to worry that her birthday would be ruined. With no time to lose, she quickly ran outside to see what had happened. When she got there, she saw a big, black cloud blocking out the sun. 

Jane knew she had to do something. She thought and thought until she came up with a plan. She ran inside and grabbed her biggest, strongest umbrella. Then she ran back outside and opened it up. 

The black cloud started to leave and the birds all flew away. Jane had saved the day! She had used her smarts and bravery to keep her special day safe. 

The moral of this story is simple: with a lot of thought and courage, you can make things right. No matter how dark it looks, always remember you can make things bright.

One day, Anna and Ben went to the park with their mom. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish. Anna and Ben wanted to feed the ducks, so mom gave them some bread.

"Look, mom, the ducks are hungry!" Anna said, throwing some bread into the water.

"Yes, they are. But be careful, don't go too close to the pond. It's very cold and the water might freeze," mom said.

"What does freeze mean?" Ben asked.

"Freeze means the water becomes hard and solid, like ice. You can't swim or drink it then," mom explained.

"Oh, I see. Does ice have a texture?" Ben wondered.

"Texture means how something feels when you touch it. Ice has a smooth and slippery texture. It's very different from water, which is wet and soft," mom said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They wanted to touch the ice and feel its texture. They looked around and saw a small fountain in the park. The water from the fountain was spraying in the air and falling on the ground. Some of the water had frozen on the grass and the rocks.

"Can we touch the ice there, mom?" Anna asked, pointing to the fountain.

"Sure, but be careful. It might be sharp and cold," mom said.

Anna and Ben ran to the fountain. They saw the ice sparkling in the sun. It had different shapes and colors. Some of the ice was clear and shiny, some was white and fluffy, and some was red and sticky.

"Wow, this ice is so pretty!" Anna said, touching the clear ice. It felt cold and smooth on her fingers.

"Look, this ice is red!" Ben said, touching the red ice. It felt sticky and wet on his hand.

"Red ice? Let me see," mom said, coming closer. She looked at the red ice and smiled. "That's not ice, Ben. That's jam. Someone must have dropped their sandwich here and the jam spilled on the ground. It didn't freeze, it just stayed red and sticky."

"Jam? Can I eat it?" Ben asked, licking his lips.

"No, Ben, don't eat it. It's dirty and old. You might get sick. Let's go wash your hand and find a clean place to eat our own sandwiches," mom said.

"Okay, mom. But can we come back and play with the ice later?" Ben asked.

"Sure, if the ice is still there. But remember, don't touch the red jam. It's not ice, it's yucky," mom said.

Anna and Ben agreed. They followed mom to the bathroom and washed their hands. Then they ate their sandwiches and drank their juice. They had a lot of fun at the park, playing with the ice and the ducks. They learned what freeze and texture mean, and they learned that not all red things are ice. They had a great day.

They waited and waited. But they did not hear any sounds from outside. They started to feel hot and stuffy in the box. They tried to push the lid, but it was too heavy.

"Help!" Tom shouted. "We are stuck!"

Anna began to cry. She was scared and wanted to go home. She said, "I don't like this game. I want to get out!"

They both began to panic. They kicked and banged on the box, hoping someone would hear them.

Meanwhile, upstairs, Mom was looking for them. She heard their noise and went to the basement. She saw the box and wondered what they were doing. She lifted the lid and saw their scared faces.

"Tom! Anna! What are you doing in there?" she asked.

They jumped out of the box and hugged her. They told her they were playing pirates and got trapped in the cave.

Mom said, "I'm glad you are OK. But you should never play in a box like that. It is dangerous and not fun. Next time, use your imagination, not a box."

Tom and Anna said they were sorry and learned their lesson. They decided to play something else, something safer and happier. They thanked Mom for saving them and gave her a kiss.

One day, a rat was looking for food in a big bin. He saw a piece of cheese and ran to get it. But he did not see the trap that was under the cheese. Snap! The trap closed on his tail and he could not move.

"Help! Help!" he squeaked. "Someone help me!"

A cat was walking by and heard the rat. He licked his lips and thought, "What a tasty snack!" He walked to the bin and saw the rat in the trap.

"Hello, little rat," he said. "Are you stuck? Do you need some help?"

The rat was very scared. He knew the cat wanted to eat him. He said, "Please, Mr. Cat, do not hurt me. I am sorry I took the cheese. I was very hungry. Please let me go."

The cat thought for a moment. He was hungry too, but he also felt sorry for the rat. He said, "All right, I will help you. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will not take any more cheese from this bin. There are other bins with better food. And you have to promise me that you will not tell anyone that I helped you. Cats and rats are not supposed to be friends."

The rat nodded and said, "I promise, I promise. Thank you, Mr. Cat. You are very kind."

The cat used his paw to reverse the trap and free the rat's tail. The rat ran out of the bin and said, "Thank you, thank you, Mr. Cat. You are the best. Goodbye!"

The cat watched the rat go and said, "Goodbye, little rat. Be careful and stay away from traps. And remember your promise."

The rat was very grateful to the cat. He kept his promise and never took cheese from that bin again. He also never told anyone that the cat helped him. He thought, "Maybe cats and rats can be friends, after all."

Lily and Spot come to Ben and Fluffy. Lily is glad that Fluffy is okay, but she is also angry with Ben.

"Yes!" Lily said.

"Stop! Stop! Stop!" they shouted.

"Yuck!" Lily said.

"Ew!" Max said.

They looked at each other and burst into laughter. They were messy, but they didn't care. They had just had the most adventurous slide ever.

Mom came running to see what had happened. She saw Lily and Max covered in pizza and smiled.

"Looks like you had a lot of fun," she said.

"We did, mom, we did!" Lily and Max said.

"Come on, let's go home and clean up. And maybe we can have some pizza for lunch," mom said.

"Yay!" Lily and Max said.

They hugged mom and walked home, still giggling. They had just had the best day ever.

She went to the kitchen and asked her mom. "Mom, can you tell me about butter?" she said.

"Sure, Sara. Butter is a food that comes from milk. Milk comes from cows. Cows are big animals that live on farms. They eat grass and hay. Do you know what grass and hay are?" her mom said.

"Yes, mom. Grass and hay are green and yellow plants. I see them when we go to the park. But how does milk become butter?" Sara said.

"Well, Sara, milk has to be shaken a lot to become butter. When you shake milk, it separates into two parts: a solid part and a liquid part. The solid part is butter, and the liquid part is buttermilk. You can use butter to make bread and cake more yummy, and you can use buttermilk to make pancakes and biscuits. Do you like pancakes and biscuits?" her mom said.

"Yes, mom. I love pancakes and biscuits. Can we make some today?" Sara said.

"Of course, Sara. We can make some for lunch. You are a lucky girl. You have a lot of books to study, and you have a lot of butter to eat. You are very smart and very sweet, just like butter." her mom said.

Sara hugged her mom and smiled. She was happy. She had learned something new about butter, and she was going to have a delicious lunch. She thought that studying was fun, and that butter was wonderful.
