Lily was sad, but she decided to help her mommy clean the house. As they were cleaning, they found a recipe for blueberry muffins. "Let's make muffins!" Lily exclaimed.

They made the muffins and they smelled delicious. Finally, the mailman arrived and they got their package. Lily was happy that her restlessness had come to an end, and she got to enjoy her delicious muffins with her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Flopsy. Flopsy loved to hop around in the fields and play with his friends. One day, while playing, Flopsy saw a shiny thing in the grass. He hopped over to it and found out it was a fake carrot. 

Flopsy was sad because he wanted a real carrot to eat. He didn't want to waste his time with a fake one. So, he hopped around some more, searching for a real carrot. Finally, he found one! It was the biggest carrot he had ever seen. He was so happy and hopped all the way back to his burrow to eat it. 

From that day on, Flopsy never wanted to play with fake things again. He knew it was a waste of time and he would rather spend his time hopping around with his friends and finding real things to enjoy.

After finding the ball, the old man smiled and Timmy's dad gave him a high five. Timmy realized that even though the old man was deaf, he was still very kind and helpful. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always be careful while playing golf and to be kind to everyone, no matter what.

The little girl looked up at the night sky and saw the terrible sight of the moon's tears. She reached up and gently wiped away his tears. 

The moon was so happy that the little girl had dried his tears that he shone down on her with his biggest and brightest smile. The little girl was so happy that her own tears turned into a huge smile too. 

And from that day forward, themoon and the little girl were always happy whenever they saw each other.

Once upon a time there was a little rabbit who had no one to play with. He was very lonely. He went for a walk and he came to a big pond. By the pond there were two ducks, who were laughing and playing together. The little rabbit felt sad and helpless. He tried to call out to the ducks but they didn't hear him. 

Suddenly the rabbit saw a jelly drop in the pond. He wanted to have the jelly, so he sharpened a stick to poke it out of the water. He tried hard and eventually he managed to get it out. But it was too slippery to hold onto and it fell back into the pond. 

The little rabbit was sad and he started to cry. But then, the two ducks saw him and came to help. They told him that if he got two sticks it would be easier to catch the jelly. So the little rabbit followed their advice and the three of them were able to get the jelly out of the water. 

The little rabbit was so delighted! He thanked the two ducks for helping him. From that day onward, the rabbit had two new friends to play with. Together, they would often go to the pond and catch jelly!

Jack stopped his bike and hopped off. He said to himself, "I should tie this switch down so it does not get lost." He took some string from his pocket and carefully wrapped it around the switch. Then he tied it into a tight knot.

Now Jack was so proud of himself. He got back on his bike and went for a ride. Every time he pressed down on the switch, it worked perfectly. Jack smiled and felt very proud of himself for tying the switch down so it would not get lost.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called John. He was 3 years old, and had just started talking. One day, John went to the park with his mom. He saw a big sack there. It was a big, rough sack and John wanted to speak to it. 
 
He said hello to the sack but it didn't answer. So John tried again, a little louder this time. He said "Hello Sack!" Still, the sack didn't answer.

John's mom smiled and said, "Maybe the sack didn't hear you, let's try again." Then she said "Hello Sack! Can you hear me?"

Suddenly, the sack moved! John was very surprised. He shouted "Mom, it answered me!" His mom giggled and said "See, even sacks can speak if you say hello loud enough." 

John smiled, then hugged the sack and said goodbye before walking home with his mom.

She walked and walked until she finally came to a small, cozy house. When she knocked on the door, an old lady opened it. She introduced herself as Auntie, and she said that she was the one who had given Lola the lemon.

Lola was so happy to finally meet Auntie! Auntie was friendly and kind, and Lola asked her to stay for tea. They talked and laughed for a long time.

Lola was very glad that she had met her dependable friend Auntie. She said goodbye and thanked Auntie for the delicious lemon. Lola had a big smile on her face all the way home!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big purple truck. The truck has a sign that says "Beef". Anna and Ben are curious.

"Can we go and see the truck?" Anna asks Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe we need to ask someone," Ben says.

They look around and see a man in a blue shirt. He is holding a clipboard. He looks busy.

"Excuse me, sir," Anna says. "Can we see the purple truck?"

The man looks at them and smiles.

"Sure, you can see the truck. But you can't touch it, okay? It's full of beef for the market. Do you know what beef is?" he asks.

Anna and Ben nod. They know that beef is meat from cows. They like to eat beef sometimes.

"Wow, that's a lot of beef!" Ben says.

"Yes, it is. Do you want to see how I load the beef into the truck?" the man asks.

"Yes, please!" Anna and Ben say.

The man permits them to follow him. He shows them how he uses a big machine to lift the boxes of beef and put them in the truck. Anna and Ben watch with wonder. They think the man has a cool job.

"Thank you for showing us, sir," Anna says.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun in the park. And remember, don't touch the purple truck!" the man says.

Anna and Ben wave goodbye and run back to the playground. They have a new story to tell their friends. They like the purple truck and the beef man.

One day, Anna's cousin Ben comes to visit. Ben likes to play and have fun. He does not care about being organized. He likes to make messes and noises. He likes to do things in different ways.

Anna and Ben go to Anna's room. Anna shows Ben her toys, her books, and her clothes. She tells him how she likes to keep them. Ben does not listen. He takes out the toys and throws them on the floor. He takes out the books and drops them on the bed. He takes out the clothes and puts them on his head.

"Stop it, Ben!" Anna says. "You are making a mess. You are not being organized. You are not doing things in order."

"I don't care, Anna!" Ben says. "I am having fun. I am being creative. I am doing things in different ways."

Anna and Ben start to argue. They raise their voices and push each other. They do not notice that Anna's mom is coming to the room. She is wearing a bathrobe and holding a towel. She has just taken a shower.

"Anna, Ben, what is going on here?" Anna's mom says. "Why are you making so much noise? Why is your room so messy?"

Anna and Ben stop arguing. They look at Anna's mom. They look at the toys, the books, and the clothes. They feel ashamed.

"We are sorry, mom," Anna says.

"We are sorry, auntie," Ben says.

Anna's mom sighs. She says, "I know you have different ways of playing, but you need to respect each other and your things. You need to clean up this mess and apologize to each other. Then you can have a snack and play something else."

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Okay, mom. Okay, auntie."

"Come on, Tom, let's go on the trail. It will be fun!" Sara said.

"No, Sara, I don't want to go. The trail is too high and too long. And it looks gloomy. There might be monsters or snakes or spiders," Tom said.

"Don't be silly, Tom. There are no monsters or snakes or spiders. And it's not gloomy, it's just shady. Mom and dad will be with us. Please, Tom, please!" Sara begged.

Tom shook his head. He did not want to go. He wanted to stay on the grass and play with his toy car. Sara was angry. She wanted to go on the trail and see what was on the other side. She decided to go by herself. She left Tom and ran to the trail.

"Bye, Tom. I'm going on the trail. You can stay here and be a baby," Sara said.

Sara started to climb the trail. She saw rocks and trees and flowers. She liked the trail. She felt brave and happy. She did not see mom and dad. They were busy talking to each other. They did not see Sara go on the trail.

Tom saw Sara go on the trail. He felt sad and lonely. He did not like to play by himself. He wanted to be with Sara. He wished he was not scared. He looked at the trail. He wondered what Sara was doing. He decided to go after her. He left his toy car and ran to the trail.

"Sara, Sara, wait for me!" Tom shouted.

Tom started to climb the trail. He saw rocks and trees and flowers. He did not like the trail. He felt scared and tired. He saw a big rock that looked like a monster. He screamed and ran back.

"Sara, Sara, help me!" Tom cried.

Sara heard Tom scream. She turned around and saw him running. She saw the big rock that looked like a monster. She laughed and ran to him.

"Tom, Tom, don't be scared. It's not a monster. It's just a rock. A silly rock. Look, I can rock it with my foot. See, it's not scary. It's funny," Sara said.

She rocked the rock with her foot. It wobbled and rolled. Tom saw that it was just a rock. He felt silly and relieved. He laughed with Sara.

"Sorry, Sara. I was scared. But you were right. It's not a monster. It's just a rock. A funny rock. Can we go back now?" Tom said.

"Sure, Tom. Let's go back. But next time, don't be scared. The trail is fun. And we can do it together," Sara said.

They held hands and went back to the grass. They saw mom and dad. They were looking for them. They were worried.

"Where were you, Sara and Tom? We were looking for you. You should not go on the trail by yourself. It's dangerous. You could get hurt or lost," mom said.

"We're sorry, mom. We wanted to go on the trail. Sara went first and I went after her. But we're okay. We saw a rock that looked like a monster. But it was not a monster. It was just a rock. A funny rock. We rocked it with our foot," Tom said.

Mom and dad looked at each other. They did not understand. They saw the rock that looked like a monster. They did not think it was funny. They thought it was scary. They hugged Sara and Tom.

"We're glad you're okay, Sara and Tom. But please, don't go on the trail by yourself again. Stay with us. We love you," dad said.

Sara and Tom nodded. They loved mom and dad. They also loved the trail. And the rock. The funny rock. They smiled and played with their toy car. They were happy.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. Sue wants to go on the slide. Tom is scared.

"Come on, Tom. The slide is fun. Don't be a baby," Sue says.

"No, Sue. The slide is too high. I don't want to fall," Tom says.

Sue does not listen to Tom. She is careless. She runs to the slide. She climbs up the ladder. She sits on the top. She smiles at Tom.

"Look at me, Tom. I am brave. I am going to slide down," Sue says.

But Sue does not see the big hole in the slide. The slide is broken. Sue slides down. She falls into the hole. She screams.

"Help, Tom. Help me. I am stuck. I am hurt," Sue says.

Tom hears Sue. He is scared. But he is also brave. He runs to the slide. He sees Sue in the hole. He grabs her hand. He pulls her out. He saves her.

"Are you okay, Sue? You are bleeding. You need a band-aid," Tom says.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. You saved me. I am sorry. I was careless. I should have listened to you," Sue says.

Tom and Sue hug. They are safe. They go to find a grown-up. They need help. They learn a lesson. They will be more careful next time.

Lila was hungry. She wanted to eat soup. She saw a big pot of soup on the stove. She did not know who made the soup. She did not care. She took a spoon and dipped it in the pot.

"Yum, yum, this soup is good!" she said to herself. She ate more and more soup. She did not hear her mom come in the kitchen.

"Lila, what are you doing?" her mom asked. She was angry. "That soup is not for you. That soup is for the sick people in the hospital. I made it for them. You should not eat unknown soup. It might make you sick too."

Lila felt bad. She wanted to say sorry. But before she could, she felt a tickle in her nose. She sneezed. She sneezed again and again. She sneezed so hard that she spilled the soup all over the floor and herself.

"Ah-choo! Ah-choo! Ah-choo!" she sneezed.

Her mom sighed. She took Lila to the bathroom. She cleaned her up. She gave her some medicine. She put her to bed.

"Lila, you learned a hard lesson today," her mom said. "You should not eat unknown soup. You should ask before you take something that is not yours. You should think of others before yourself. Maybe next time, you can help me make soup for the sick people. That would be a nice thing to do."

Lila nodded. She felt sorry. She felt sick. She hoped the sick people would get better. She hoped she would get better too. She closed her eyes and tried to sleep.

The end.

Lily liked to question everything. She always asked her mom and dad why things were the way they were. Sometimes they had answers, sometimes they did not. Lily wanted to learn more about the world.

One day, Lily saw a strange fruit in the kitchen. It was wrinkled and dark and looked like a raisin, but bigger. She picked it up and asked her mom, "What is this?"

"That is a prune, Lily. It is a dried plum. Some people like to eat them as a snack," her mom said.

"Why is it dried?" Lily asked.

"Because it lasts longer that way. And it is sweeter and softer than a fresh plum," her mom said.

"Can I try it?" Lily asked.

"Sure, but be careful. It has a pit inside. You have to spit it out," her mom said.

Lily took a bite of the prune. She liked the sweet taste, but she felt something hard in her mouth. She spit out the pit and looked at it. It was small and brown and had a crack in it.

"What is this?" Lily asked.

"That is the seed of the plum, Lily. If you plant it in the ground, it can grow into a plum tree," her mom said.

"Really? Can we plant it?" Lily asked.

"Well, it is not that easy, Lily. You need a lot of space and water and sun and time for a plum tree to grow. And not all seeds will sprout. It is a modest chance," her mom said.

Lily did not understand what modest meant, but she wanted to try anyway. She asked her mom if she could have a pot and some soil and some water. Her mom agreed and helped her plant the pit in the pot. She told her to put it in a sunny spot and water it every day.

Lily did as her mom said. She was very curious and hopeful. She wondered if the pit would grow into a plum tree. She checked on it every day, looking for signs of life. She asked her mom when it would sprout. Her mom said it could take weeks or months or even years. She said it was a miracle of nature.

Lily did not give up. She kept watering and watching and waiting. She did not know it, but her mom was very proud of her. She thought Lily was a patient and persistent and modest girl.

One day, after many days, Lily saw something green poking out of the soil. She was so excited and happy. She ran to her mom and said, "Look, look, mom! The prune pit sprouted! It is a plum tree!"

Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Yes, Lily, it is. You did it. You grew a plum tree from a prune pit. That is amazing. You are amazing."

Lily beamed and thanked her mom. She said, "Can we eat the plums when they grow?"

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. But it will take a long time for the plums to grow. You have to keep taking care of the tree and watching it grow. It will be a long and wonderful journey."

Lily nodded and said, "I will, mom. I will. I love the prune pit tree. And I love you."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love your questions. They make you smart and curious and modest. Never stop questioning, Lily. Never stop learning."

Lily likes to sing. She sings when she wakes up, when she plays, when she eats, and when she goes to bed. She sings happy songs, sad songs, silly songs, and made-up songs. She sings with her toys, her mom, her dad, and her cat.

One day, Lily sings a new song. She sings about a lucky star. She sings that the lucky star can make wishes come true. She sings that she wants to see the lucky star and ask for a wish. She sings that she loves the lucky star and hopes it loves her too.

That night, Lily looks out of her window. She sees many stars in the sky. They are bright and shiny and pretty. She looks for the lucky star. She thinks it must be the biggest and brightest star of all. She finds a star that looks like it. She smiles and sings her song to the star.

The star hears Lily's song. It likes her song. It likes her voice. It likes her too. It twinkles and sparkles and sends a beam of light to Lily's window. It tells Lily that it is the lucky star and that it can make her wish come true. It asks Lily what she wishes for.

Lily thinks for a moment. She has many things that she likes. She likes her toys, her mom, her dad, and her cat. She likes to sing, to play, to eat, and to sleep. She is happy and grateful for what she has. She does not need anything more. She tells the star that she wishes for the star to be happy and to have a friend. She tells the star that she is its friend and that she will sing to it every night.

The star is touched by Lily's wish. It is the kindest and sweetest wish it ever heard. It thanks Lily for being its friend and for singing to it. It tells Lily that it will always be happy and that it will always listen to her songs. It tells Lily that she is the luckiest girl in the world and that it will always watch over her.

Lily and the star say good night to each other. Lily goes to bed and falls asleep. She dreams of the star and the star dreams of her. They are both happy and lucky and they both love to sing.

The driver said, "I looked around. I thought someone was playing a joke on me. But there was no one. Only the lions. And one of them was looking at me. He had a big mane and yellow eyes. He opened his mouth and said, 'Thank you.'"

Lily and Tom said, "Wow!"

The driver said, "I was shocked and scared. I did not know what to do. I did not know how to answer. I ran away and closed the door. I told my boss what happened. He did not believe me. He said I was crazy. He fired me. He said I could not work at the zoo anymore. He said I had to find another job. So I became a bus driver. And that's why I love the zoo. Because it reminds me of the lion who said, 'Thank you.'"

Lily and Tom said, "That's amazing!"

The driver said, "Yes, it is. And maybe, if you are lucky, you will see him today. And maybe, he will say, 'Thank you' to you too."

Lily and Tom smiled. They hoped they would see the lion who said, 'Thank you'. They thanked the driver for his story. They got off the bus and ran to the zoo. They had a wonderful day. And they never forgot the driver and his secret.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a shiny jewel on the ground. Sara picked it up and said, "Look, Tom, I found a jewel! It is so pretty and sparkly!"

Tom wanted the jewel too. He said, "No, Sara, it is mine! I saw it first! Give it to me!" He tried to grab the jewel from Sara, but she held it tight.

They started to fight over the jewel. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They did not see the old lady who was sitting on a bench nearby. She was watching them with a sad face.

She walked over to them and said, "Children, why are you fighting over this jewel? Do you know where it came from?"

Sara and Tom stopped fighting and looked at her. They said, "No, we don't know. We just found it on the ground. Why do you ask?"

The old lady said, "This jewel belongs to me. I dropped it by accident when I was walking here. It is very special to me. It was a gift from my husband who passed away. He gave it to me on our wedding day. It is the only thing I have left of him."

Sara and Tom felt sorry for the old lady. They realized that they were being selfish and greedy. They said, "We are so sorry, ma'am. We did not know. Here, take your jewel back. We are sorry for fighting over it."

The old lady smiled and thanked them. She said, "You are very kind, children. Thank you for giving me back my jewel. I hope you learned a lesson today. It is not good to fight over things that are not yours. It is better to share and be happy with what you have. And remember, the most precious jewels are not the ones that shine, but the ones that love."

Sara and Tom nodded and hugged the old lady. They said, "We understand, ma'am. Thank you for teaching us. We will not fight over things anymore. We will share and be happy with what we have. And we will love each other as twins."

Sara and Tom said, "We will, ma'am. Goodbye and take care."

One day, a little otter was playing by the river. He liked to swim and catch fish and slide on the rocks. He saw a big rope hanging from a tree. He thought it looked fun to swing on it.

He swam to the rope and grabbed it with his paws. He tried to swing, but the rope was too long. He did not know how to make it shorter. He saw a knot on the rope. He thought maybe he could untie it and make the rope shorter.

He pulled and twisted the knot with his teeth. But he did not know how to untie it. He only made it tighter. The knot got stuck on his neck. He could not breathe. He tried to call for help, but no one heard him.

"Help, help!" he gasped. "I can't breathe!"

A big bear was walking by the river. He heard the otter's cry. He looked up and saw the otter hanging from the rope. He thought the otter looked tasty. He climbed the tree and reached for the otter.

"Please, don't eat me!" the otter begged. "I'm stuck! Please, help me!"

The bear did not care. He grabbed the otter and bit him. The otter felt a lot of pain. He closed his eyes and stopped breathing.

The bear ate the otter and licked his lips. He thought the otter was unusual. He had never eaten an otter with a rope around his neck before. He shrugged and walked away.

"OK, let's go," Lily says.

They run to the house and find Mom in the kitchen.

"Mom, Mom, can you help us? We want to make a house for our toys, but Sam won't share his tools with us. He is mean," Tom says.

Mom listens to them and smiles.

"Of course, I can help you. I have some tools you can use. They are not big and heavy like Sam's, but they are good for your project. Come with me," Mom says.

She takes them to the garage and gives them a small wheelbarrow and a small shovel. She also gives them some glue and some paint.

"Here you go. You can use these tools to make your house. But be careful and don't hurt yourselves. And don't make a mess," Mom says.

"Thank you, Mom. You are the best," Tom and Lily say.

"Look, look, we made a house. It is strong and pretty. We used our tools and our skills," Tom says.

They all play together and have fun.

They are friends and siblings.

One day, a curious frog saw a big hole in the ground. He wanted to know what was inside, so he hopped closer and closer. He did not see the snake that was hiding in the hole, waiting for a snack.

"Hello, little frog," the snake said with a smile. "Do you want to play with me?"

The frog was scared of the snake, but he did not want to show it. He pretended to be brave and said, "Yes, I want to play with you. What game do you have?"

The snake said, "I have a fun game. It is called hide and seek. You hide, and I seek. If I find you, you are mine. If I don't find you, you are free. Do you want to try?"

The frog thought for a moment. He did not like the sound of the game, but he did not want to say no. He thought he could find a good hiding place and escape from the snake. He said, "OK, I will play with you. But you have to count to ten first."

The snake agreed and started to count. The frog quickly hopped away and looked for a hiding place. He saw a big rock, a tall grass, and a small pond. He decided to hide in the pond, because he thought the snake would not look there. He jumped into the water and hid under a lily pad.

The snake finished counting and started to look for the frog. He searched under the rock, but he did not find him. He searched in the tall grass, but he did not find him. He searched around the pond, but he did not find him. He was getting angry and hungry. He decided to look in the pond, too.

He slithered into the water and looked under the lily pads. He saw the frog hiding there, and he smiled. He said, "I found you, little frog. You are mine now. You should not have played with me. You should have run away."

The frog was terrified and realized his mistake. He wished he had listened to his mother, who always told him to stay away from strangers. He said, "Please, don't eat me, Mr. Snake. I am sorry I played with you. I will never do it again. Please, let me go."

The snake said, "No, I will not let you go. You are my lunch. You should have been more careful and not so curious. Curiosity can be dangerous, little frog. Goodbye."

The snake opened his mouth and swallowed the frog in one gulp. He felt satisfied and happy. He said, "That was a tasty frog. I like playing hide and seek. Maybe I will find another frog to play with tomorrow."

The end.

Moral: Be careful of strangers and don't let your curiosity get you into trouble.

"But we don't want to play in our bedroom. We want to play in the garden. We want to run and jump and splash in the puddles," Lily said.

"I'm sorry, honey, but you have to wait until the rain stops. Maybe you can read a book or draw a picture or sing a song," mom said.

Tommy and Lily sighed. They did not like to read or draw or sing. They wanted to play. They went back to their bedroom and sat on the floor. They looked at their toys and the window and the rain.

Then, they heard a noise. It was a knock on the window. They looked up and saw a bird. It was a colorful bird with a long tail and a playful eye. It tapped on the glass and made a funny sound.

"Hello, bird!" Tommy said.

"Hello, hello, hello!" the bird said.

Tommy and Lily gasped. The bird could talk!

"Who are you? Where did you come from?" Lily asked.

"I'm Polly. I came from the tree. I saw you looking sad and I wanted to say hi," the bird said.

"Wow, you're amazing! Can you come in and play with us?" Tommy asked.

"Sure, I can. But you have to open the window first," the bird said.

Tommy and Lily ran to the window and opened it. Polly flew in and landed on their bed. She looked around and saw their toys.

"Ooh, what are these? Can I try them?" she asked.

"Of course, you can. They are our toys. We have cars and dolls and balls and books. You can play with anything you like," Lily said.

"Yay, thank you! You are very nice. Let's play together!" Polly said.

Tommy and Lily smiled. They forgot about the rain and the boredom. They played with Polly and their toys. They laughed and talked and had fun. They were happy.

Mom heard the noise and came to their bedroom. She saw them playing with the bird and smiled.

"Look, mom, this is Polly. She can talk and she's our friend. She came to play with us," Tommy said.

"Hello, mom. I'm Polly. I'm a playful bird. I like your kids. They are fun," Polly said.

Mom was surprised and amused. She was glad that Tommy and Lily found a way to enjoy their day.

"That's wonderful, sweetie. I'm happy for you. Polly, you're welcome to stay as long as you like. But be careful not to make a mess," mom said.

"OK, mom. Thank you, thank you, thank you!" Polly said.

Mom left them to play and went back to the kitchen. She looked out the window and saw that the rain had stopped and the sun had come out. She smiled and thought that it was a good day after all.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They were very happy and jolly. But then Tom noticed a big dog. The dog was barking and running towards them. Tom was scared. He ran away from the dog, but he tripped and fell. He hurt his knee and it was bleeding.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. Lily ran to him and hugged him. She saw his knee and said, "Don't cry, Tom. I have a bandage in my bag. I will help you."

Lily took out a bandage and wrapped it around Tom's knee. She kissed it and said, "There, there. It will be better soon. You are very brave, Tom."

Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind, Lily. You are my best friend."

Lily smiled and said, "You are welcome, Tom. You are my best friend too."

They hugged and then they saw the dog again. But the dog was not scary anymore. He was wagging his tail and licking his owner's hand. The owner was a nice lady who said, "I'm sorry, kids. My dog was just excited to see you. He is very friendly and gentle. Do you want to pet him?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other and nodded. They petted the dog and he licked their faces. They laughed and said, "He is very jolly, too."

The end.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see what was up there.

"Can we climb the tree, please?" Anna asked her mom.

"Be careful, okay? And don't go too high," her mom said.

Anna and Ben nodded and ran to the tree. They found a low branch and pulled themselves up. They felt the warm sun on their faces and the cool breeze on their hair. They saw many birds and bugs and flowers. They felt a lot of wonder.

"Look, Ben, a nest!" Anna said, pointing to a small basket of twigs and feathers.

"Wow, maybe there are eggs inside!" Ben said, moving closer to the nest.

"Wait, Ben, don't touch it!" Anna said. "The birds might get mad."

But Ben did not listen. He reached out his hand and touched the nest. Suddenly, a loud squawk filled the air. A big bird flew out of the nest and flapped its wings. It looked angry and scared.

"Yield, yield!" the bird cried. "This is my home, go away!"

Anna and Ben were frightened. They let go of the branch and fell to the ground. They ran to their mom and hugged her.

"Sorry, mom, we didn't mean to make the bird mad," Anna said.

"It's okay, sweeties, you didn't know," her mom said. "But next time, you should respect the animals and their homes. They have feelings too, you know."

Anna and Ben nodded. They learned a lesson that day. They decided to play somewhere else and leave the bird in peace. They still liked the tree, but they knew it was not theirs to touch.

Sara and Ben stop and look at the duck. They feel sorry for making noise and fighting. They look at the rock and see how beautiful it is.

But one day, a man came to the park. He wore a white coat. He had a badge. He looked angry. He saw Anna and Ben with Spot. He ran to them.

"That's not a toy. That's an intelligent robot. I made it. It's very expensive. You stole it from my lab. You're in big trouble!" he said.

Anna and Ben were scared. They did not know what to do. They did not mean to steal. They thought it was a toy. They just wanted to play. They loved Spot.

"Maybe you're right. Maybe Spot is happier with you. Maybe he needs friends. Maybe I was too busy to play with him. Maybe I was wrong." he said.

He opened the plastic box. He gave Spot back to Ben. He smiled.

"OK, you can keep him. But you have to promise me something. You have to take good care of him. You have to respect him. You have to learn from him. He's not just a toy. He's an intelligent robot. He can teach you many things. He can help you grow. He can make you better." he said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They hugged Spot. They thanked the man. They promised him. They were very happy. They learned a lesson. They learned to be honest. They learned to be grateful. They learned to be kind. They learned to smile.

Timmy groaned, but he knew his mom was right. He began to pick up his toys and put them in their proper spots. As he was cleaning, he found a shiny copper penny on the ground. "Look Mommy!" he exclaimed, holding up the penny. "I found a penny!"

"That's very exciting, Timmy," said his mom. "But remember, it's important to keep your toys organized so you can find them easily next time you want to play with them."

Timmy nodded and finished cleaning up his toys. From then on, he made sure to keep his toys organized so he could find them easily. And every time he found a shiny penny, he knew it was a special treat for being responsible.

Later that day, Lily went outside to play with her friends. They were having a picnic and playing games. Lily's friend, Tommy, accidentally spilled some juice on her dress. But that was fine, because Lily's mommy had packed an extra dress for her to wear. 

After a fun day of playing, Lily went home and cuddled with Fluffy. She thought about how much she loved her toys, her friends, and her cat. And she knew that even though things might not always be perfect, everything would be fine in the end.

Fluffy woke up and saw the water on the floor. She jumped off the armchair and walked over to Sarah. Fluffy started to lick the water off the floor, helping Sarah clean up the mess. Sarah smiled and said, "Thank you, Fluffy!" And from that day on, Fluffy and Sarah became the best of friends.

One day, a gray comet named Gary was speeding through the sky. Gary was very fast, and he liked to race with his friend, the wind. They would laugh and play as they raced each other.

"Let's see who is faster today," said the wind.

"Okay!" replied Gary, and they started to speed through the sky.

As they raced, they saw a little bird who was flying slowly. The bird was sad because he could not fly as fast as Gary and the wind.

"Hi, little bird," said Gary. "Why are you sad?"

"I can't fly as fast as you and the wind," said the bird.

Gary felt bad for the bird, so he had an idea. He asked the wind to help him make the bird fly faster. The wind blew behind the bird, and the bird started to speed up.

"Wow! I'm flying so fast!" said the happy bird. "Thank you, Gary and wind!"

From that day on, Gary, the wind, and the bird became good friends, and they raced together in the sky.

The next day, Lily went to Sally and said, "I am sorry for asking for your necklace. I should not have done that. Can we still be friends?" Sally smiled and said, "Of course we can!" Lily learned that it's not nice to be envious of others and that being a good friend is more important than having things.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to the park with his mom. Timmy wore a black shirt and pointed to the big slide. "Mommy, can we go on the slide?" he asked. His mom said yes and they climbed up the ladder to the top.

When they got to the top, Timmy saw something shiny. "Look, mommy! Silver!" he shouted. His mom looked and saw a silver coin on the ground. "That's lucky," she said, and Timmy picked it up.

As they went down the slide, Timmy held the silver coin tightly. "I'm going to keep this forever," he said. When they got to the bottom, Timmy pointed to the swings. "Can we go on the swings now?" he asked. His mom smiled and said, "Sure thing, Timmy." And they swung back and forth, happy as can be.

"Of course! Let me kneel down and take a look at it," John said as he got down on his knees.

John smiled and replied, "No problem, neighbor. It's always good to help each other."

Bee and Bear were friends. Bee liked to make honey in her home. Bear liked to eat honey from her home. But Bee did not like to share all her honey with Bear. She worked hard to make it.

One day, Bee saw Bear coming to her home. He was hungry and wanted honey. Bee flew out and said, "Stop, Bear! This is my honey. You can have some, but not all. If you take too much, I will sting you. That will hurt a lot. Do you understand?"

Bear nodded. He did not want to hurt Bee or get stung. He liked Bee as a friend. He said, "Okay, Bee. I understand. I will only take a little honey. Thank you for sharing."

Bee smiled. She was happy that Bear listened to her. She said, "You're welcome, Bear. But be careful. The honey is in a tight jar. You have to open it slowly and gently. If you open it too fast or too hard, it will break. Then the honey will spill and make a mess. Do you understand?"

Bear nodded again. He did not want to break the jar or make a mess. He said, "Okay, Bee. I understand. I will open it slowly and gently."

Bee flew back to her home. She watched as Bear opened the jar. He did it slowly and gently, just like Bee said. He took a little honey and licked his paw. He smiled. The honey was sweet and yummy. He said, "Thank you, Bee. This is good honey. You are a good friend."

Bee smiled back. She was glad that Bear enjoyed the honey and was a good friend. She said, "You're welcome, Bear. You are a good friend, too. But remember, this is my honey. You can have some, but not all. And always open the jar slowly and gently. Or I will sting you."

Bear nodded. He remembered what Bee said. He said, "I will, Bee. I will. Don't worry."

They both laughed. They were happy. They were friends.

"Why are you doing this?" Mia asked.

"Trust me," Tom said. "This will make the dog go away. Come on, let's go to the door."

Mia did not understand, but she did what Tom said. She followed him to the door, where the dog was still barking and scratching.

"See?" Tom said. "He thinks you are hurt. He won't hurt you. He wants to be your friend."

Mia was amazed. She looked at Tom and smiled. She looked at the dog and wagged her tail. She was not fearful anymore. She was curious.

They run to the rock. Lily goes first. She climbs on the rock. She gains some height. She can touch the lowest apple. She picks it and smiles.

"Yay, I got one!" she says. "Here, Tom, catch!"

She throws the apple to Tom. Tom catches it. He is happy. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are smart."

Lily says, "You are welcome, Tom. You are good at catching."

They are about to eat their apples, when they hear a voice.

"Hey, you two, what are you doing?"

They turn around. They see a man. The man is angry. He says, "That's my tree. Those are my apples. You are stealing from me."

Lily and Tom are scared. They say, "Sorry, sir. We didn't know. We were hungry."

The man says, "That's no excuse. You have to pay me for the apples. Give me your money."

Lily and Tom say, "We don't have money. We are kids."

The man says, "Then give me something else. What do you have?"

Lily and Tom look at each other. They don't have much. Lily has a doll. Tom has a wallet. His dad gave him the wallet. It is empty, but it is shiny and blue.

The man sees the wallet. He says, "Give me that wallet. It looks nice. Maybe it has some money inside."

Tom doesn't want to give his wallet. He likes his wallet. He says, "No, sir. This is my wallet. My dad gave it to me. It is special."

The man says, "I don't care. Give it to me, or I will call the police."

Lily and Tom are more scared. They don't want to go to the police. They don't know what to do. They are stuck.

The witch sees them. She smiles a wicked smile. She says, "Hello, my little ones. Do you want to come in? I have some candy for you. And some soup. It is perfect for you."

Anna and Ben are scared. They know the witch is lying. They want to run away. But they are too close to the house. The witch opens the door. She reaches out her hand. She tries to grab them.

Anna and Ben scream. They turn around and run. They stumble on a root. They fall to the ground. They hurt their knees. They cry. The witch laughs. She walks towards them. She says, "Don't cry, my little ones. I will make you feel better. Come with me."

Anna and Ben are very scared. They think the witch will eat them. They wish they never came to the woods. They wish they stayed at home. They wish their mom and dad were here.

But then, they hear a bark. They see a dog. It is their dog, Spot. Spot is big and strong. He likes to play with Anna and Ben. He follows them to the woods. He sees the witch. He does not like the witch. He growls and barks. He runs to Anna and Ben. He protects them.

The witch is angry. She does not like the dog. She says, "Go away, you nasty dog. You are ruining my perfect plan. I will turn you into a frog."

She raises her hand. She has a stick. It is her wand. She points it at Spot. She says a magic word.

But nothing happens. The wand does not work. It is broken. The witch is confused. She looks at the wand. She sees a bite mark. Spot bit the wand. He broke the magic.

The witch is furious. She yells and screams. She throws the wand. She tries to catch Spot. But Spot is faster. He jumps and bites the witch. He bites her nose. He bites her hat. He bites her dress.

The witch is in pain. She cries and begs. She says, "Stop, stop, please stop. You are hurting me. Let me go. I will leave you alone. I will never bother you again."

Anna and Ben are happy. They hug Spot. They say, "Thank you, Spot. You are our hero. You saved us from the witch. You are the best dog ever."

They get up and run. They leave the woods. They go back to their home. They tell their mom and dad what happened. They show their knees. They are scratched and bruised. But they are not bleeding. They are not bad.

Their mom and dad are worried. They say, "We are glad you are safe. But you should not go to the woods alone. You should not talk to strangers. You should not go near the witch's house. It is dangerous. You could get hurt. Or worse."

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "We are sorry, mom and dad. We were curious. We were foolish. We will not do it again. We learned our lesson. We will listen to you. We will be careful."

Their mom and dad hug them. They say, "We love you, Anna and Ben. We are proud of you. You are brave and smart. And you have a good friend. Spot is a good dog. He loves you too. He deserves a treat."

They give Spot a bone. He wags his tail. He licks their faces. He is happy. He is a good dog.

Anna and Ben smile. They say, "We love you too, Spot. You are our perfect dog. You are our perfect friend."

Suddenly, a big bird flew over them and scared Mittens. She ran away and got lost. She couldn't find her way back home. She cried out for help, but nobody came to find her. She was lost and alone, and she didn't know what to do. Poor Mittens never saw her family again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved her rabbit. Her rabbit was white and fluffy, and Lily loved to play with it every day. One day, Lily went to the store with her mommy to buy some carrots for her rabbit. When they got to the store, Lily saw a toy she really wanted. It was a cheap toy, but her mommy said they didn't have enough money to buy both the toy and the carrots.

Lily was sad and didn't want to leave the store without the toy. She said to her mommy, "I want the toy, but I don't want to forget about my rabbit. What should I do?" Her mommy said, "We can't buy both, so we have to choose. What's more important to you, the toy or your rabbit?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "My rabbit is more important. I don't want to forget about him." So, they bought the carrots for her rabbit and went home. Lily played with her rabbit and was happy that she didn't forget about him. She realized that sometimes, the things we want are not as important as the things we already have.

That night, Amy tried what the old lady said. She shut her eyes and thought of her happy place. Then, she said, "I will have a good sleep tonight." And guess what? It worked! Amy had the most successful sleep and no more nightmares.

The lady tried to find a way to make the people increase their quietness. She thought for a long time and finally had an idea. She walked around the restaurant and gave every person a marshmallow.

The people were confused at first, but the lady explained that if everyone held a marshmallow in their mouths, it would decrease the noise in the restaurant. So everyone put a marshmallow in their mouths and sure enough, it kept them quiet.

The people in the restaurant were so happy that the lady had found a way to make the noise decrease. They thanked her and from that day forward, everyone in the restaurant kept their marshmallows close by!

"Hello, children. What are you doing?"

They looked up and saw an elderly man with a long beard and a hat. He was smiling at them.

"Why do you want to pull it?" the man asked.

"We want to make a fort," Mia said.

The man nodded. "I see. Well, I have a secret for you. This log is not just a log. It's a magic log. It can grant you one wish, if you know how to ask."

Ben and Mia gasped. They had never heard of a magic log before.

"Really?" Ben asked.

"Really," the man said. "But you have to be careful what you wish for. Sometimes, you get more than you bargained for."

"We wish for a big cake!"

The angry man came closer and closer. He looked around, but he did not see the first man or the children. He only saw the ball, lying on the grass. He thought the ball belonged to the first man. He picked up the ball and threw it away. He hoped the first man would run after it.

But the first man did not run after the ball. He stayed behind the tree with Ben and Lily. He smiled and thanked them.

"You are very brave and kind," he said to them. "You saved me from the bad man. He cannot find me now. I can go to my new home safely. Thank you very much."

Ben and Lily smiled back. They were happy they helped the first man. They did not need the ball anymore. They had a new friend.

Ben says, "I think so. But we have to share it. And we have to throw away the seed. It's too big to eat."

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a white dove in a tree. The dove had a shiny ring on its leg.

"Look, a dove!" Tim said. "It is so pretty!"

"Maybe it is a wild dove," Sam said. "Maybe it can fly very far."

They wondered where the dove came from and where it was going. They wanted to see it up close. They tried to climb the tree, but it was too high.

"Let's get some bread," Tim said. "Maybe the dove will come down if we give it some bread."

They ran to the house and got some bread. They broke it into small pieces and threw them on the ground. They waited for the dove to come down.

But the dove did not come down. It stayed on the branch and looked at them. It did not seem hungry or scared.

"Come on, dove!" Tim said. "We just want to be your friends!"

"Maybe it does not like bread," Sam said. "Maybe it likes something else."

They wondered what else the dove might like. They looked around and saw some flowers, some seeds, some water, and some shiny things.

"Let's try these," Sam said. He picked up some flowers and some seeds and threw them on the ground. Tim picked up some water and some shiny things and threw them on the ground.

They waited for the dove to come down. But the dove did not come down. It stayed on the branch and looked at them. It did not seem interested or curious.

"Why won't you come down, dove?" Tim said. "Don't you want to play with us?"

"Maybe it is not a wild dove," Sam said. "Maybe it belongs to someone."

They wondered who the dove belonged to and why it had a ring on its leg. They looked at the ring and saw some letters and numbers on it.

"Maybe the ring has a name or a number," Tim said. "Maybe we can call someone and find out."

They ran to the house and got a phone. They tried to read the ring, but it was too small and far away.

"Let's get some binoculars," Sam said. "Maybe we can see better with them."

They ran to the house and got some binoculars. They looked through them and saw the ring clearly. It had a name and a number on it.

"Look, it says Mike and 555-1234," Tim said. "Maybe Mike is the dove's owner."

"Let's call Mike and tell him we found his dove," Sam said. He dialed the number and waited for someone to answer.

"Hello, this is Mike," a voice said.

"Hello, Mike," Sam said. "We found your dove. It is in a tree near our house. It has a ring on its leg with your name and number."

"Really? That's great!" Mike said. "Thank you so much for finding my dove. It is a racing dove. I sent it on a race, but it got lost. I was worried about it."

"A racing dove?" Sam said. "What is that?"

"It is a dove that can fly very fast and far," Mike said. "It can find its way back to its home by following a map in its head. But sometimes it gets confused or tired and needs some help."

"Wow, that's amazing!" Sam said. "Can we see it fly?"

"Sure, if you want," Mike said. "I'll come over and get it. Where do you live?"

Sam told Mike his address and hung up. He and Tim ran outside and waited for Mike. They looked at the dove and wondered how it could fly so fast and far. They hoped it would be happy to see Mike.

Soon, Mike arrived in his car. He had a cage and a whistle. He thanked Sam and Tim for finding his dove and walked to the tree. He blew his whistle and called the dove's name.

"Come on, Snowy, come on!" Mike said.

The dove heard Mike's voice and whistle. It recognized him and flew down from the branch. It landed on Mike's shoulder and cooed softly. Mike smiled and stroked its feathers. He put it in the cage and closed the door.

"Good boy, Snowy, good boy!" Mike said. "You did a great job. I'm so proud of you."

He turned to Sam and Tim and said, "Do you want to see him fly?"

"Yes, please!" Sam and Tim said.

Mike opened the cage and let the dove out. He blew his whistle and pointed to the sky.

"Go, Snowy, go!" Mike said.

The dove flapped its wings and soared into the air. It circled around and flew higher and higher.

"Hello, Lily," said a voice. Lily turned and saw a lady. The lady had a kind face and a long dress. She was holding a book. "What are you painting?" the lady asked.

"I'm painting a rainbow for Sam. He is sick and I want to make him happy," Lily said.

"That's very compassionate of you, Lily. Do you know what compassionate means?" the lady asked.

Lily shook her head. She did not know that word.

"Compassionate means you care about others and want to help them. You are a compassionate friend, Lily. Can I teach you something about rainbows?" the lady asked.

Lily nodded. She liked to learn new things.

The lady opened her book and showed Lily a picture. It had a rainbow and some words. The lady pointed to the words and said, "These are the names of the colors in the rainbow. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. Can you say them with me?"

Lily repeated the words after the lady. She liked how they sounded. She looked at her colors and tried to match them with the words.

"Very good, Lily. You are a smart painter. Do you know why we see rainbows?" the lady asked.

Lily shook her head again. She did not know that either.

"Rainbows are made by sunlight and water. When the sun shines on the water droplets in the air, they act like tiny prisms. They split the sunlight into different colors. And we see them as a rainbow. Isn't that amazing?" the lady explained.

Lily nodded. She thought that was amazing. She looked at the sky and the rainbow again. She felt happy and grateful.

"Thank you for teaching me, lady. You are very nice. What is your name?" Lily asked.

"My name is Iris. I am the goddess of rainbows. I like to visit children who love rainbows and teach them about them. You are a special child, Lily. I have a gift for you," Iris said.

She touched Lily's paper and made it sparkle. She gave it to Lily and said, "This is a magic rainbow. It will always make you and Sam happy. And it will remind you of me and our lesson. Goodbye, Lily. Keep painting and being compassionate."

Lily hugged the paper and thanked Iris. She watched as Iris disappeared in a flash of colors. She ran to Sam's house and gave him the magic rainbow. Sam smiled and hugged Lily. Mommy went to the garden and saw the spider. She said, "Don't be nervous, Lily. The spider is not going to hurt you. Let's watch it together and learn about it." 

Lily and her mommy watched the spider together and learned that it was not scary after all. They even gave it a name, "Spidey". From that day on, Lily was not nervous anymore when she saw Spidey in her garden.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Finn. Finn loved to swim in the ocean with his friends. One day, Finn saw a shiny line in the water. He asked his friend, "What's that?" His friend said, "It's a fishing line. We should stay away from it so we don't get caught."

Finn was an honest fish and wanted to warn all his fish friends about the line. He shouted, "Everyone, there's a fishing line in the water! Stay away!" 

Suddenly, a seagull flew down and tried to catch Finn. Finn quickly dove into the water to escape. He was safe, but scared. Finn realized that sometimes it's important to be honest and warn others, even if it means diving into danger.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot liked to play outside in the woods. One day, Spot was walking near a river when he saw a big log in the water. Spot wanted to play with the log, so he jumped in the river to get it. But the current was too strong, and Spot got hurt. 

Spot tried to swim back to the shore, but he couldn't. He started to bark for help. Luckily, a brave firefighter named Tim was nearby. Tim heard Spot's barks and came to rescue him. Tim jumped in the river and swam to Spot. He grabbed the log and helped Spot get back to the shore. 

Spot was very happy to be safe and sound. He wagged his tail and licked Tim's face to say thank you. Tim smiled and patted Spot's head. From that day on, Spot never played near the river again. He knew that it was dangerous, and he didn't want to get hurt again.

Just then, a kind grasshopper saw her struggling and offered to help carry the salt. The little ant was grateful and realized that it's okay to rely on others sometimes. Together, they loaded the salt onto the grasshopper's back and brought it to the ant's home. 

From that day on, the little ant learned that being independent doesn't mean doing everything alone, and that sometimes asking for help is the best thing to do.

So, they made a tent together, and Timmy was so happy. He went back to his friends and asked if he could join them again. This time, they said yes, and they all had fun playing together in the tent.

The moral of the story is that it's okay to get dirty when you play, and you should always include others and let them join in on the fun.

Soon, Max's teeth began to hurt. He cried and cried. His mommy took him to the doctor. The doctor said Max's teeth were hurt because he chewed on the log. Max was sad and wished he had listened to his mommy.

The moral of the story is to always listen to your mommy and daddy, because they know what is best for you.

His mom says, "Ben, why don't you pray for your robot? Maybe God can help your robot work again."

Ben does not know what pray means. He asks his mom, "What is pray?"

His mom says, "Pray is when you talk to God. You can tell God what you want, what you need, what you are thankful for, or what you are sorry for. God listens to you and loves you. He can do anything."

Ben likes the idea of talking to God. He says, "Okay, mom, I will pray for my robot."

Her mom says, "I don't know, Lily. Maybe it is hiding. Let's look for it together." They search the house, but they still cannot find it. Lily starts to cry.

Then, her dad comes home. He has a serious face. He says, "Lily, I have something to tell you. I accidentally took your duck to work. I thought it was my phone. I'm sorry."

Lily is surprised. She says, "You took my duck to work? How did you do that?"

Her dad says, "I was in a hurry and I grabbed the wrong thing. But don't worry, I brought it back. Here it is." He gives her the pink duck. It is a little dirty, but it still quacks.

Lily is very happy. She hugs her dad and says, "Thank you, dad. I missed my duck. Can we bathe now?"

Her dad says, "Of course, Lily. Let's go." They go to the bathroom and fill the tub with water and bubbles. They put the duck in and bathe together. They splash and sing and make the duck swim. They are very happy.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toy farm. They had cows, pigs, sheep and a horse. They liked to make noises and pretend they were farmers. Sara had a wool hat that she wore to keep warm. Ben had a red tractor that he drove around.

One day, they saw a huge truck outside their house. It had a big sign that said "Wool". They ran to the window and watched. The truck driver got out and opened the back. He took out big bags of wool and put them on a cart. He pushed the cart to the door and rang the bell.

Sara and Ben's mom opened the door. She smiled and thanked the truck driver. She took the bags of wool and brought them inside. She told Sara and Ben that she had ordered the wool to make sweaters and blankets for them. She asked them if they wanted to help her.

Sara and Ben nodded and followed their mom to the living room. There, she had a big basket with needles and yarn. She showed them how to knit and crochet. She gave them each a small ball of wool and a needle. Sara and Ben tried to copy their mom. They made loops and stitches with the wool.

They had fun making things with the wool. Sara made a scarf for her doll. Ben made a hat for his horse. They showed their mom what they had made. She praised them and hugged them. She said they were very clever and creative. She gave them each a kiss and a cookie.

Sara and Ben were happy. They liked playing with their toy farm, but they also liked making things with wool. They blinked their eyes and smiled. They wondered what else they could make with wool. They decided to make a blanket for their cow. They picked up their needles and wool and started to work.

Lily liked to jog with her dad. They jogged every morning in the park. They saw many things when they jogged. They saw birds, flowers, dogs, and people.

One day, they jogged past a farm. Lily saw a big field of corn. The corn was yellow and tall. Lily wanted to touch the corn. She asked her dad if she could.

"OK, but be careful," her dad said. "Don't go too far."

Lily ran to the corn. She felt the leaves and the ears. She saw a purple thing in the corn. It was a butterfly. The butterfly was pretty. It had purple wings and spots. Lily wanted to catch the butterfly.

She followed the butterfly into the corn. She forgot about her dad. She forgot about the park. She only saw the butterfly. She ran and ran.

"Lily, where are you?" her dad called. He was worried. He could not see Lily. He could not hear Lily. He ran into the corn. He looked for Lily.

Lily heard her dad. She stopped running. She saw the butterfly fly away. She was sad. She wanted the butterfly. But she also wanted her dad. She called him.

"Dad, I'm here!"

Her dad heard her. He ran to her. He hugged her. He was happy. He was also angry.

"Lily, you scared me!" he said. "You should not run away like that. You could get lost. You could get hurt. You should stay with me."

Lily was sorry. She did not mean to scare her dad. She did not mean to run away. She only wanted the butterfly.

"I'm sorry, dad," she said. "I saw a purple butterfly. It was pretty. I wanted to catch it."

Her dad understood. He liked butterflies too. He was not angry anymore. He smiled.

"I know, Lily," he said. "Butterflies are pretty. But they are also free. They like to fly. They do not like to be caught. You can look at them. You can admire them. But you should not chase them. You should jog with me."

Lily nodded. She learned her lesson. She hugged her dad. She jogged with him. They jogged back to the park. They saw many things when they jogged. They saw birds, flowers, dogs, and people. And they saw more butterflies. But they did not chase them. They jogged with them.

After a while, Lily saw the dog's owner come and lock him up in a cage. Lily felt safe again and climbed down from the tree. She knew that the dog would not be able to hurt her anymore. From that day on, whenever Lily saw the fierce dog in the park, she would climb up a tree and watch from above.

She knew what was coming. She tried to hold it in, but she couldn't. She sneezed so hard that her button popped off her shirt and flew into the tree where the squirrel was. The squirrel grabbed the button and ran away.

Lily was sad that she lost her button, but she was happy that the nosy squirrel was gone. She learned that sometimes things happen for a reason, and she shouldn't be too nosy herself.

The moral of the story is that even if someone is not kind to you, you can still be kind to them and make them happy.

After a while, the traffic had stopped and they were able to move along. The mom and the young girl were feeling impatient, but the elderly man knew that being patient would pay off in the end.

Moral of the story: Patience is a virtue. No matter the situation, if you wait patiently, it will be better in the end.

One day, a little bird was flying in the sky. He saw a big tree with many fruits. He wanted to eat some, but he was afraid of the other birds. They were bigger and louder than him.

He flew closer and saw a wise old owl sitting on a branch. The owl looked at him and said, "Hello, little bird. Do you want some fruits?"

The little bird nodded and said, "Yes, please. But the other birds are scary. They might hurt me."

The owl smiled and said, "Don't be afraid, little bird. You have a gift that they don't have. You can scatter the seeds of the fruits and make new trees grow. That is a good thing to do. The other birds only eat and waste the fruits. They don't care about the future."

The little bird was amazed and said, "Really? I can do that?"

The owl said, "Yes, you can. Just take a fruit and fly away. Then, find a distant place where there is no tree. Drop the seed on the ground and cover it with some dirt. Then, come back and do it again. Soon, you will see new trees growing and more fruits for everyone."

The little bird thanked the owl and did what he said. He took a fruit and flew away. He found a distant place where there was no tree. He dropped the seed on the ground and covered it with some dirt. Then, he came back and did it again.

The other birds saw him and laughed. They said, "Look at that silly bird. He is wasting the fruits. He is not smart like us. He is not strong like us. He is not brave like us."

But the little bird did not mind. He knew he was doing a good thing. He learned from the owl's wisdom. He was happy and proud.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes, the smallest and quietest ones can make the biggest and loudest difference.

Daisy and Tom tried to move the rock together, but it was still too heavy. They didn't give up. They asked more friends to help. Finally, with everyone's help, they moved the rock. Daisy's mom saw them and said, "I'm proud of you, Daisy. You didn't give up and worked together with your friends."

The moral of the story is that when we work together, we can do things we couldn't do alone.

Happy was not sure if he would like the spicy treat. But he wanted to be a good friend, so he said, "Yes, I accept your gift, Chirpy."

Happy took a bite of the spicy treat. At first, it was very hot in his mouth. Happy's eyes grew big, and he started to feel very warm. Chirpy could see that Happy was feeling hot from the spicy treat.

Chirpy had a plan. "Wait here, Happy. I will be right back!" Chirpy flew away and came back with a big, cold drink for Happy. Happy drank the cold drink, and it made him feel much better.

Polly and Tim spent the day together. They practiced tying knots with a rope. At first, Tim was not very good at it. But Polly was patient and showed him again and again. Soon, Tim was able to tie knots just like Polly.

Tim was very happy and said, "Thank you, Polly, for teaching me how to tie knots. You are a great friend." Polly smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tim. I'm glad I could help you."

From that day on, Tim and Polly became best friends. They played together every day and tied many knots. And they lived happily ever after.

Lily and Tom were twins who lived on a farm. They liked to play with the animals and help their mom and dad. One day, they saw something weird in the barn. It was a big pile of snow with a hat and a carrot on top.

"Look, it's a snowman!" Lily said. "Who made it?"

"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe it was the cows. They like to play, too."

They ran to the barn and hugged the snowman. He was cold and wet, but they did not mind. They gave him a name: Bob.

"Hi, Bob!" they said. "Do you want to play with us?"

But Bob did not say anything. He just smiled with his carrot mouth.

Lily and Tom played with Bob for a long time. They sang songs, told jokes, and made him a scarf out of hay. They had a lot of fun.

But then, the sun came out. It was warm and bright. Lily and Tom felt hot and thirsty. They decided to go inside and get some water.

"Bye, Bob!" they said. "We'll be back soon. Don't go anywhere!"

But Bob did not say anything. He just smiled with his carrot mouth.

Lily and Tom went inside and drank some water. They also ate some cookies and milk. They felt better and wanted to play with Bob again.

They ran to the barn and looked for Bob. But they could not find him. All they saw was a small puddle of water, a hat, a carrot, and a scarf.

"Where's Bob?" Lily asked. "What happened to him?"

Tom looked at the sun. He looked at the water. He looked at the hat. He understood.

"Bob melted," he said. "He was made of snow, and snow melts when it's hot."

Lily felt sad. She liked Bob. He was a good friend.

"Can we make him again?" she asked.

Tom nodded. He liked Bob, too.

"Yes, we can," he said. "But we have to wait for winter. Then, there will be more snow, and we can make Bob again."

Lily smiled. She felt better.

"Okay," she said. "Let's wait for winter. Then, we'll make Bob again, and play with him, and have fun."

They took the hat, the carrot, and the scarf, and put them in a safe place. They said goodbye to Bob, and thanked him for playing with them. They hoped he would come back soon.

They ran to their mom and dad, and told them about Bob. They said he was a weird snowman, but a nice one. They said they would make him again in winter.

Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them. They said they were proud of them, and that they had big imaginations. They said they loved them, and that they were happy.

Lily and Tom smiled and hugged them back. They said they loved them, too, and that they were happy.

They were a happy family.

"Tom is not bad, Lisa," Mom said. "He is just a baby. He does not know better. He wants to play with you. He loves you."

Lisa looked at Mom and Tom. She saw Mom smile at Tom. She saw Tom snuggle with Mom. She felt a pang in her heart.

She loved Mom too. She wanted Mom to smile at her. She wanted Mom to snuggle with her. She felt envious.

"Mom, do you love me?" Lisa asked.

Mom looked at Lisa. She saw her sad eyes. She put Tom down. She opened her arms.

"Of course I love you, Lisa," Mom said. "You are my big girl. You are my helper. You are my sweetie."

She hugged Lisa and kissed her cheek.

"Can you love me and Tom?" Lisa asked.

Mom nodded.

"I can love you and Tom," Mom said. "I have enough love for both of you. You are my children. You are my treasures."

Lisa smiled. She felt better. She hugged Mom back.

"Can I play with Tom?" Lisa asked.

Mom smiled.

"Sure, you can play with Tom," Mom said. "But you have to mind him. You have to be gentle and kind. You have to share and teach. You have to be a good sister."

Lisa nodded.

"I will mind Tom," Lisa said. "I will be a good sister. I love Tom too."

She took Tom's hand. She gave him a doll. She showed him how to play.

Tom stopped crying. He giggled. He played with Lisa.

Mom watched them. She felt happy. She loved Lisa and Tom. They were her family.

One day, they decided to explore the other side of the woods, where they had never been before. They saw many new things, like a pond, a bridge, and a cave. They were curious and excited.

"OK, Tom, but be careful. It might be dark and cold," Jen said.

They walked towards the cave, holding hands. As they got closer, they felt a chill in the air. They shivered and hugged each other.

"Tom, I don't like this. Let's go back," Jen said.

He took a step into the cave, but Jen pulled him back.

"Tom, no! It's not a cat or a bear. It's a monster!" Jen said.

She pointed to the cave and screamed. Tom looked and saw a pair of glowing eyes and sharp teeth. It was a monster, and it was angry.

They agreed, and they never did. They still played in the woods, but only near the oak tree, where they felt safe and happy.

Lily was very upset and started to cry. Her mom came in and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about the ink and how it ruined her story. Her mom tried to comfort her by saying they could buy a new notebook, but Lily was still sad.

From that day on, Lily was too scared to write any more stories. She kept her notebook locked away in the cabinet and never wrote again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cocoa so much that she asked her mommy to make her some every day. One day, while Lily was drinking her cocoa, she accidentally spilled it on her shirt. 

"Oh no!" cried Lily. "My shirt is dirty now."

"Don't worry, Lily," said her mommy. "We can wash it and make it clean again."

"I wish I could own a shirt that never gets dirty," said Lily.

"That would be nice," said her mommy. "But for now, let's just clean this one."

Lily smiled and finished her cocoa, happy that she had a mommy who knew how to make things clean again.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the zoo with her mom. She loved to see all the different animals, but her favorite was the elephant. She thought the elephant was very attractive, with its big ears, long trunk and gray skin.

"Mom, can I serve the elephant some food?" Lily asked. "Please, please, please?"

"Sure, honey, but you have to be careful and follow the rules," her mom said. "The zookeeper will show you what to do."

Lily was very happy and followed her mom to the elephant enclosure. There, they met the zookeeper, who had a big bucket of fruits and vegetables.

"Hello, I'm Sam, and this is Ellie, our elephant," the zookeeper said. "She is very friendly and smart, but also very strong and hungry. Do you want to serve her some food?"

"Yes, please!" Lily said.

"Okay, then, listen carefully. You have to stand behind this fence and hold the food in your hand. Then, you have to say 'Ellie, trunk up!' and she will lift her trunk. Then, you have to toss the food into her mouth. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and took a banana from the bucket. She held it in her hand and said "Ellie, trunk up!" Ellie lifted her trunk and opened her mouth. Lily tossed the banana and Ellie caught it. She chewed it and made a happy sound.

"Good job, Lily!" Sam said. "You served the elephant very well. Do you want to try again?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She took another fruit and repeated the process. She served the elephant several times, and each time Ellie thanked her with a sound or a nudge.

Lily had a lot of fun serving the elephant. She felt very proud and happy. She thanked Sam and Ellie and gave them a hug. Then, she went to see the other animals with her mom. But she always remembered the attractive elephant and how she served her food.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big pile of coal near the train tracks. They wanted to touch it and see what it was like.

"Let's go and play with the coal!" Tom said.

"No, we should not do that. Mom said coal is dirty and can hurt us." Sam said.

But Tom did not listen to Sam. He ran to the coal and grabbed a handful. He felt the coal was hard and black. He rubbed it on his face and laughed.

"Look at me, I am a coal man!" Tom said.

Sam shook his head and stayed away from the coal. He saw a man coming from the train. The man was wearing a hat and a jacket. He had a whistle in his mouth.

"Hey, you! What are you doing with my coal?" The man shouted.

Tom was scared and dropped the coal. He tried to run away, but the man caught him. He looked at Tom's face and clothes. They were all covered with coal.

"You are a naughty boy! You should not play with coal. It is not a toy. It is for the train. It makes the train go fast and strong. And it is spicy. It can burn your skin and eyes if you are not careful." The man said.

He took Tom to a faucet and washed his face and hands. He gave him a towel and a scolding. He told him to go home and say sorry to his mom.

Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He wished he had listened to Sam. He walked home with Sam, who was kind to him.

"Are you okay, Tom?" Sam asked.

"Yes, I am okay. But I learned a lesson. Coal is not for playing. It is spicy and dirty and can hurt us. We should listen to mom and not touch things we do not know." Tom said.

Sam nodded and hugged Tom. He was glad Tom was okay. He hoped Tom would be more careful next time.

The end.

Moral value: We should listen to our parents and not play with things that can harm us.

Lily and Ben were brother and sister. They liked to play in the garden, but today it was raining. They were bored and sad.

"Let's play hide and seek in the house," Ben said. "You count to ten and I hide."

"Okay," Lily said. She closed her eyes and counted. "One, two, three..."

Ben ran to find a good hiding place. He saw a big closet in the hall. He opened the door and went inside. He shut the door behind him. It was dark and quiet.

"Nine, ten," Lily said. "Ready or not, here I come!" She looked for Ben in the living room, the kitchen, the bathroom, but she could not find him. She wondered where he was.

She went to the hall and saw the closet. She thought Ben might be there. She reached for the door, but then she heard a loud noise. It was a thunder. She was scared of thunder. She jumped back and ran to the sofa. She hid under a blanket.

Ben heard the thunder too. He was scared of thunder. He wanted to get out of the closet, but he could not. The door was stuck. He pushed and pulled, but it did not move. He was trapped. He shouted for help.

"Lily, Lily, where are you? I'm in the closet. Help me!"

Lily heard Ben's voice. She felt sorry for him. She was still scared of thunder, but she loved her brother. She got out of the blanket and went to the closet. She tried to open the door, but it was hard. She used all her strength and finally opened it.

Ben saw Lily's face. He was happy and relieved. He hugged her and thanked her.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to scare you. I was scared too."

"It's okay, Ben. I'm sorry too. I didn't mean to leave you. I was scared too."

They smiled at each other and walked to the sofa. They cuddled under the blanket and waited for the rain to stop. They sighed and hoped the sun would come out soon.

Anna loves to watch the otters at the zoo. They are brown and furry and swim fast in the water. One day, she sees a big otter teaching a small otter how to catch a fish. The big otter holds the fish in its paws and shows the small otter how to bite it. The small otter tries to do the same, but drops the fish. The big otter picks it up and gives it back to the small otter.

"Good try, little one," the big otter says. "You will learn soon. Fish are yummy and good for you."

Anna smiles and claps her hands. She wants to talk to the otters. She leans over the fence and says, "Hello, otters. You are very smart and cute. Can I be your friend?"

The otters hear Anna and look at her. They see her red hair and blue eyes and hear her nice voice. They swim closer to the fence and make noises. They sound like they are saying hello back.

"Hi, Anna," the big otter says. "We are happy to see you. You are very kind and pretty. You can be our friend."

Anna is surprised and happy. She did not know otters can talk. She says, "Thank you, otters. You are very friendly and fun. Can I learn from you?"

The otters nod and smile. They say, "Yes, Anna. You can learn from us. We can teach you many things. How to swim, how to play, how to be happy."

Anna is excited and curious. She says, "That sounds great, otters. I want to learn from you. Can I come with you?"

The otters say, "Yes, Anna. You can come with us. But you need to be careful. The water is deep and cold. And you need to ask your mom and dad first."

Anna agrees and runs to find her mom and dad. She tells them about the otters and asks them if she can go with them. Her mom and dad are surprised and worried. They say, "Anna, are you sure? Otters are wild animals. They live in a different world. They might not be safe for you."

Anna says, "Please, mom and dad. The otters are nice and smart. They want to be my friends. They want to teach me. Please let me go with them."

Her mom and dad look at each other and sigh. They love Anna and want her to be happy. They say, "Okay, Anna. You can go with the otters. But only for a little while. And you have to wear a life jacket and stay close to us. And you have to listen to the otters and do what they say. Do you understand?"

Anna nods and hugs her mom and dad. She says, "Thank you, mom and dad. I understand. I will be careful and have fun. I love you."

She puts on a life jacket and follows the otters to the water. They welcome her and teach her how to swim, how to play, how to be happy. Anna learns a lot and has a lot of fun. She feels like she is part of the otter family. She is glad she met the otters and became their friend.

Tom and Lily are twins. They are six years old. They go to school every day. They like to learn new things and play with their friends.

One day, their teacher tells them they have to take an exam. An exam is a test that shows what they know. Tom and Lily are a little scared. They do not like exams. They think exams are hard and boring.

The teacher gives them a paper with questions and a pencil. They have to write the answers. Tom and Lily look at the paper. They do not know some of the questions. They feel sad and confused.

They look at each other. They have an idea. They move their chairs closer. They whisper in their ears. They decide to help each other. They share their answers. They think they are smart and clever.

The teacher sees them. She is angry. She walks to their desks. She takes their papers and pencils. She says, "Tom and Lily, you are cheating. Cheating is bad. You have to do the exam by yourself. You have to be honest and fair. If you cheat, you do not learn anything. You have to take the exam again. And you have to pay for a new paper and pencil. They are expensive. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nod. They feel sorry and ashamed. They say, "We are sorry, teacher. We will not cheat again. We will try to do the exam by ourselves. We will pay for the paper and pencil. We will learn from our mistake."

The teacher nods. She gives them a new paper and pencil. She says, "Good. I hope you do better this time. And remember, cheating is not worth it. It only makes you lose. Learning is fun and rewarding. It makes you grow."

Ben did not listen. He wanted to keep the saw. He thought it was fun and cool.

"Come on, Lila," he said. "Don't be a baby. Let's go cut some branches and make a fort!"

Lila did not want to go. She wanted to be loyal to Ben, but she also wanted to be safe and good. She had to make a choice.

She looked at Ben and the saw. Then she looked at the park and the people. She knew what to do.
